articles.title: Crypto Bug Bounty Platforms Are Fighting AI Spam With AI
articles.text:
AI is driving a flood of crypto bug reports. Now it’s helping sort them
Bug bounty platform HackerOne said it’s increasing its triage throughput with AI agents after a record quarter of reports in the third quarter.
Crypto bug bounty platforms have expanded their use of artificial intelligence to keep up with a growing mountain of AI-assisted security reports.
Crypto-focused HackenProof said in October that it was using AI to triage 70% of submissions fully autonomously, aiming to hit 85% by the end of 2026. It said it received an average of about 6,100 bug reports a month in the third quarter, 2.4 times the reports from December last year.
Rival Immunefi last week said submissions to its platform rose 136% year-over-year in the first nine months of 2026, as it introduced a tool that can flag duplicates before a researcher submits a report.
Bug bounty programs pay independent researchers to find and report potential security flaws. AI has helped researchers uncover more genuine vulnerabilities, but has also swelled the volume of invalid and duplicate submissions, making it harder for security teams to identify the threats that need urgent attention.
It’s like “bringing a sword to a gunfight,” Dmitry Tokarev, founder of crypto wallet provider Bron, told Cointelegraph, referring to security teams that haven’t already adopted AI to sift through reports.
The turning point for AI-assisted bug hunting
Several bug bounty platforms have identified February as a turning point in the surge of AI-assisted vulnerability reports, coinciding with the release of more capable AI models, including Anthropic’s Claude Opus 4.6.
HackenProof said Claude Opus 4.6 could work through larger codebases and sustain tasks for longer. HackerOne said the arrival of more capable AI models and tools in that month saw a sudden shift from a “human-only submission environment.”
Some crypto developers are also experimenting with financial disincentives to curb low-quality submissions.
The team behind Firedancer, a Solana validator client developed by Jump Crypto, which also uses AI to screen reports, took an additional measure in October.
To deter spam, it began requiring researchers to burn 1 SOL for each bug report they want considered for a bounty. The token is permanently destroyed, even if the report turns out to be a duplicate.
In a November update published Tuesday, HackerOne’s vice president of operations Tony Lee said they began requiring researchers to verify their identities before submitting reports in the third quarter. It also expanded its triage team and began using AI agents to automatically close clear-cut cases, such as spam and duplicate reports.
In October, it gave customers more control over how many reports their public programs receive.
Related: AI labs likely sitting on cryptography ‘bombshells,’ computer scientist says
Security teams brace for more bug reports and attacks
Lee said he expects vulnerability reports to keep climbing “for the foreseeable future” after recording a 22% increase in report volume in Q3 compared to the previous quarter.
Meanwhile, insurer QBE and risk consultancy Control Risks on Wednesday forecast more disruptive cyber incidents in 2027 across the 14 markets they studied, pointing to the “industrialization of AI” as one of the factors.
Mike Blank, chief product officer at blockchain infrastructure firm R3, also said he expects the number of hacks to rise sharply in 2027, but said crypto teams should pay closer attention to how much damage a single breach can cause, rather than the number of attacks.
“The real difference will be between protocols where a stolen key can drain everything and those where it can only pause operations,” Blank said.

articles.title: Monero Delisted by KuCoin as Grayscale Doubles Down on Zcash
articles.text:
Privacy coins face diverging fortunes as KuCoin moves to drop Monero
As KuCoin joins exchanges dropping Monero ahead of new EU restrictions, Grayscale argues that Zcash’s privacy design sets it apart.
Crypto exchange KuCoin said Thursday it will delist Monero (XMR) on Nov. 30, making it the second major platform this month to drop the privacy coin. Exchange MEXC suspended XMR spot trading and delisted its perpetual futures contracts earlier in November.
KuCoin has already suspended XMR deposits and plans to close withdrawals on Dec. 31. XMR fell 10.5% to $449.98 as of 7:00 p.m. UTC on Thursday. The drop extends a decline from about $625 on Nov. 3.
The delisting comes as the European Union prepares to restrict privacy coins on regulated platforms. Starting July 10, 2027, the bloc’s Anti-Money Laundering Regulation will prohibit financial firms, including crypto asset service providers, from maintaining anonymous accounts or accounts that obscure transactions through “anonymity-enhancing coins,” regardless of whether the privacy features are enabled by default or optional. The regulation does not prohibit individuals from holding privacy coins in self-custody wallets.
Launched in 2014, Monero conceals transaction amounts and the wallet addresses of senders and recipients by default. Unlike Monero, Zcash (ZEC), launched in 2016, allows users to choose between transparent and shielded transactions. Both cryptocurrencies have faced regulatory scrutiny over the past few years, with Binance delisting Monero in 2024 and Kraken ending support for it in the European Economic Area later that year.
Zach Pandl, head of research at Grayscale, which launched the first US spot ZEC exchange-traded fund (ETF) in August, said Zcash is positioned differently from Monero. He told Cointelegraph that the firm’s commitment to Zcash will continue for “many years to come.”
Delistings mount ahead of EU privacy coin restrictions
KuCoin’s delisting of Monero follows a series of similar moves by crypto exchanges amid growing regulatory pressure on privacy coins. Since 2018, when Japan’s Financial Services Agency pressed exchanges to drop anonymity coins, regulators in other jurisdictions, including South Korea and Dubai, have also taken steps to restrict their use or availability.
In Europe, plans to restrict privacy coins emerged as early as 2022, when a leaked draft of an Anti-Money Laundering bill came to light. The EU’s regulation defines “anonymity-enhancing coins” as cryptocurrencies with built-in features that anonymize transaction data “either systematically or optionally,” which could bring cryptocurrencies with opt-in privacy features, such as Zcash, within the scope of the restrictions.
Related: Bitwise seeks Texas Stock Exchange listing for Zcash ETF
Pandl said that viewing keys allow Zcash holders to disclose transactions “to an auditor or regulator, law enforcement if they need.” He said the feature gives users greater control over who can access their financial information. “That is exactly how the financial system works today. It’s just that it gives the authority to individuals rather than institutions,” he said.
However, whether viewing keys alone can satisfy regulatory requirements remains a point of debate.
Other approaches to privacy are gaining traction among traditional financial institutions looking to use public blockchains. In April, Paris-based digital asset infrastructure provider Dfns partnered with cryptography firm Zama to bring confidential transactions to its more than 400 enterprise clients, including banks, fintechs and custodians. The collaboration uses encryption to conceal transaction amounts and balances on public blockchains while allowing authorized parties to access the information for compliance purposes.
Grayscale says shielding beats obfuscation
Grayscale has offered exposure to ZEC since the launch of its Zcash Trust in 2017, based on the view that transaction privacy would be essential for financial institutions to adopt public blockchains.
Pandl said that as AI has advanced, it has become “much easier to link pseudonymous addresses with offchain information.” Monero, he explained, uses ring signatures that obscure the source of transactions among multiple possible signers, a method Pandl said “may be vulnerable” as AI-powered blockchain analytics improve.
“We believe strongly that Zcash is the stronger tech,” he said, because “it takes a shielding approach rather than an obfuscation approach.” Zcash uses zero-knowledge proofs to verify shielded transactions without publicly revealing sensitive transaction data onchain.
Monero developers, however, are working on an upgrade that would replace ring signatures with a zero-knowledge proof system in a bid to enhance transaction privacy.
“For public blockchain technology to become a mainstream part of the financial system, it absolutely needs a privacy layer,” Pandl said.
ETF conviction despite outflows
Grayscale’s Zcash ETF began trading on NYSE Arca on Aug. 25, following the conversion of its Zcash Trust. While investors seeking to use Zcash’s privacy features would need to hold the cryptocurrency directly, “the ETF can provide the store of value use case of these [privacy] technologies,” Pandl said.
Grayscale’s ETF reached $1 billion in assets under management on Sept. 24, but that figure had fallen to $406 million on Wednesday. Zcash more than tripled in value this year, rising to $1,653 on Sept. 26 from $524 on Jan. 1, according to Token Terminal data. Its price more than doubled in the month following the ETF’s launch but has since fallen back to $770. The cryptocurrency remains up about 50% year to date.
Pandl described Zcash’s price appreciation over the past year as “Bitcoin’s Solana moment,” referring to Solana’s growing market cap and its challenge to Ethereum’s dominance as the “leading smart contract platform.”
“At 1.2% of Bitcoin’s market cap, I would still consider Zcash at a relatively low value,” he said, adding that Grayscale has no price targets for ZEC.

articles.title: ‘Very Racist’ Netflix SBF Series, BitMart’s $319M Shortfall: Asia Express
articles.text:
‘Very racist’ Netflix SBF series, BitMart’s $319M shortfall: Asia Express
Netflix’s The Altruist has been slammed for its ‘very racist’ portrayal of CZ. BitMart reportedly has a $319.5 million shortfall and just $1.9M in liquid assets.
Ex-FTX COO calls out Netflix over CZ’s ‘Asian mafia’ portrayal
Former FTX chief operating officer Constance Waing has slammed Netflix’s portrayal of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao in The Altruists as racist, saying it relied on Asian mafia stereotypes.
“It’s very racist,” Waing told Cointelegraph. The Altruists is a dramatization of the rise and fall of Sam Bankman-Fried’s FTX crypto empire and his subsequent imprisonment for fraud.
Waing took issue with one scene in which FTX founder SBF and Alameda CEO Caroline Ellison enter through a back door to meet CZ, saying it suggested he was “trying to get these two innocent people into something bad.”
In another episode the fictional CZ urges SBF to give Alameda Research advance access to FTX customer orders so it can trade ahead of them, a suggestion the real CZ labelled “insane.” Ethereum creator Vitalik Buterin said the portrayal exaggerated Zhao’s accent and questioned whether it was racist.
Woke 1 may have been crazy, but racist is still racist says Vitalik Buterin.
SOUTH KOREA
South Korean exchanges halt CYBER transfers amid suspected bridge exploit
South Korean crypto exchanges Upbit and Bithumb suspended deposits and withdrawals of CYBER on Sunday after the project reported suspicious activity involving its cross-chain bridge.
On Saturday, Cyber said it detected unexpected minting of CYBER tokens on Solana, followed by a transfer of tokens out of its bridge’s Ethereum lockbox. Cyber, formerly CyberConnect, operates an Ethereum layer-2 network designed for social applications.
The project said it was investigating the incident and advised users to avoid using the bridge or depositing CYBER to exchanges while the investigation continues.
South Korea proposes bank-led stablecoins, 20% cap on crypto exchange stakes
South Korea’s Financial Services Commission (FSC) unveiled a draft bill Tuesday that would initially limit issuance of won-denominated stablecoins to groups majority-owned by banks and generally cap shareholders’ stakes in crypto exchanges at 20%.
The draft also seeks to lift South Korea’s 2017 ban on domestic initial coin offerings.
The 20% ownership rule is set to affect a deal that Naver struck for Upbit owner Dunamu. The deal gave Naver full control, but under the new rules shares above the 20% cap would lose their vote.
South Korea’s crypto bill could move stablecoin race beyond token issuance
South Korean fintech companies could gain influence in bank-led stablecoin groups by signing up partners that help people spend won-denominated tokens, Tiger Research said in its Tuesday report.
“Those relationships are likely to matter more to the business than the volume of stablecoins issued,” the Asia-focused research company said.
NORTH KOREA
US seeks to recover $1.1B in crypto stolen in North Korea-linked Binance hack
The US Department of Justice is seeking to recover more than $1.1 billion in crypto stolen from cryptocurrency exchange Binance in October by North Korean hackers.
In a court filing Monday, prosecutors asked a federal court in Washington, DC, to permanently forfeit the funds, which are held in the USDC stablecoin. Since the attack, US authorities said they have helped to freeze, seize or return nearly $3 billion of the more than $6 billion taken from Binance.
JAPAN
Japan’s SBI, SMFG launch Solana venture for stablecoins, tokenization
Japanese financial giants SBI Holdings and Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) have launched a joint venture with the Solana Foundation to tokenize assets, develop stablecoin payment infrastructure and expand onchain financial services across Asia.
More news from Japan
Japan’s Financial Services Agency has published briefing materials considering proposals to regulate apps and sites that connect to DeFi, and whether to discourage access to protocols that lack money laundering controls.
Daiwa has completed a technical verification in which AI agents processed natural language instructions to screen various DEX options and to conduct stablecoin and security token swaps.
HONG KONG
Source: Pexels
Hong Kong launches tokenized debt platform with 24-hour settlement
The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) launched a platform Wednesday that supports round-the-clock settlement of tokenized debt securities in multiple currencies.
The CMU Digital Asset Platform, developed and operated by CMU OmniClear Limited on behalf of the HKMA, uses cash tokens for payment and connects with conventional payment systems and central bank digital currencies.
HK pushes to bring crypto custodians, advisers under licensing rules
Hong Kong has published a bill that would bring crypto custodians, advisers and other virtual asset service providers under mandatory licensing or registration.
On Friday, the government officially published its Virtual Asset Services Legislation (Amendment) Bill 2026, proposing that firms carrying out those activities would need to obtain a license from, or register with, the Securities and Futures Commission (SFC). The bill is set for its first reading in the Legislative Council on Dec. 2.
More news from Hong Kong
BlackRock has launched its first tokenized money market fund in Hong Kong and the Asia-Pacific region. It allows investors to use new HK stablecoin HKDAP to subscribe and redeem from the fund which offers a constant net asset value.
SINGAPORE
The Monetary Authority of Singapore has clarified that an on-chain token is not automatically a bank deposit. It draws a line between genuine tokenized deposits and crypto-like bearer instruments.
A UK court has approved an asset recovery settlement totaling 55 million pounds from Su Haijin and Xu Haika, two defendants in Singapore’s largest money-laundering case. Haika is being forced to sell 16 London apartments held through affiliated companies to repay the funds. The August 2023 police operation saw crypto worth more than S$38 million seized.
CHINA
According to Nikkei Asia, Bitmart has a $319.5 million shortfall but just $1.9 million in liquid assets available for customer repayments. Numerous users report they have been unable to access their accounts.
Bitmart disclosed the figures to Alvarez & Marsal, which is overseeing the restructuring process. The collapse highlights the dangers of high yield crypto products, with Chinese investors reportedly drawn to the platform by short term savings products offering 18.8% annualized yields for 14 day deposits.

articles.title: Today in Crypto: Spain’s Crypto Freeze Powers, Wallet Security and AI Risks
articles.text:
Here’s what happened in crypto today
Need to know what happened in crypto today? Here is the latest news on daily trends and events impacting Bitcoin price, blockchain, DeFi, Web3 and crypto regulation.
Today in crypto, Spain introduced measures that would allow authorities to suspend crypto transactions over suspected financial crimes, Vitalik Buterin advocated for greater transparency in chip design to improve hardware wallet security, and a computer scientist warned that advances in AI could threaten existing cryptographic systems.
Spain moves to grant financial watchdog power to freeze crypto accounts
A decree published on Nov. 25 would give Spain’s financial intelligence unit, Sepblac, the power to freeze crypto accounts and halt transactions without prior judicial authorization when it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing.
The measures are scheduled to take effect on Jan. 25, 2027. Under Spain’s Constitution, the Congress of Deputies must vote to ratify or repeal the decree within 30 days of its promulgation. If ratified, crypto companies operating in Spain would have to comply with suspension orders or face financial penalties.
According to the decree, Sepblac would be able to suspend the use of a digital asset account or a business relationship for up to five business days, while transactions in progress could be held for up to 10 business days. Although the initial suspension of an account or transaction would be at the discretion of Sepblac, it could be extended by a court at the request of public prosecutors.
Nikolai Timofejev, head of licensing and regulatory affairs at legal consulting firm Prifinance, told Cointelegraph that crypto firms should start preparing for the change before it takes effect. “My advice is to treat it like an operational workstream with a named person who receives Sepblac’s orders,” he said. “Non-compliance amounts to a very serious infringement attracting fines starting at €150,000.”
Vitalik Buterin calls for verifiable chips as hardware wallet threats evolve
Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin on Thursday called for enhanced verifiability in computer chips, citing evolving security threats in the hardware wallet sector.
Buterin said in a blog post that most commercial open-source chips do not disclose enough detail to verify their physical construction. Publishing what a chip is programmed to do is different from providing a blueprint against which inspectors can check the hardware itself.
“This concern is not just theoretical,” Buterin said, adding that the crypto industry has seen attacks that involve inserting spy implants into hardware wallets before they get sold to consumers.
Buterin warned that future attacks could be harder to detect, with malicious functions built into replacement chips that resemble legitimate ones.
“This, you cannot detect with the naked eye,” he wrote.
AI labs likely sitting on cryptography ‘bombshells,’ computer scientist says
Theoretical computer scientist Scott Aaronson says leading AI laboratories are likely sitting on undisclosed breakthroughs in cryptography.
In a blog post on Wednesday, Aaronson, a former OpenAI researcher and professor at The University of Texas at Austin, warned that algorithms emerging from AI-driven mathematical advances will eventually break currently deployed cryptosystems.
“I’m virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells in that area,” Aaronson said. “However, until I either see details or hear directly from someone at a lab, I feel much, much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells.”
The remarks add to concerns that AI’s accelerating mathematical capabilities could eventually undermine the cryptography used to secure crypto wallets and blockchain transactions. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and researcher Justin Drake raised those concerns in October.

articles.title: BNB Chain Publishes Litepaper for Next-Generation Network
articles.text:
BNB Chain details new layer-1 for trading, private finance and AI
The proposed network will operate alongside BNB Smart Chain and retain BNB as its native token, with a public testnet targeted for the first quarter of 2027.
BNB Chain has outlined plans for a new layer-1 blockchain designed to support high-frequency trading, payments, private financial transactions and autonomous artificial intelligence (AI) agents.
According to a litepaper published Thursday, the network would operate alongside the existing BNB Smart Chain (BSC) and use BNB as its native token, with no new native token planned. The blockchain is currently running as a development network, with BNB Chain targeting a public testnet launch in the first quarter of 2027 and a mainnet launch in the second half of the year.
On general-purpose blockchains, applications typically compete for block space. The proposed network would reserve a portion of its transaction capacity for specific activities, such as payments services, which BNB Chain said could reduce competition for network resources during periods of high demand.
The proposed network would also feature an optional shielded pool designed to support private transfers involving BNB and other supported tokens, including certain decentralized finance (DeFi) transactions. Some transaction details would remain publicly visible, and BNB Chain’s documentation warns that the pool’s circuits remain unaudited and that it should not be used with real funds.
Other proposed features would allow users to transact without first acquiring BNB to pay network fees and authorize AI agents to execute transactions within predefined limits.
Magazine: Binance’s $6.5B freeze order, Hong Kong ‘suspicious’ of HYPE: Asia Express

articles.title: Binance Completes Withdrawal Recovery Following Record Crypto Hack
articles.text:
Binance completes withdrawal recovery four weeks after $6.3B hack
The announcement concludes a phased withdrawal recovery that began on Nov. 1, when Binance restored Bitcoin withdrawals following the record crypto theft.
Binance said Thursday it had lifted all withdrawal suspensions related to its October hack, four weeks after an attack drained $6.3 billion in funds from the exchange in the largest cryptocurrency theft on record.
In an announcement, Binance said withdrawals had resumed across nearly all networks, with a small number remaining temporarily suspended due to maintenance or planned upgrades unrelated to the hack.
The exchange’s network status page shows partial deposit and withdrawal suspensions for several cryptocurrencies. USDC withdrawals, for instance, remain suspended on Hedera and World Chain due to low hot wallet balances and on Sonic due to security issues.
Binance warned users against phishing attempts, saying it would never request passwords or seed phrases or offer expedited withdrawals. The exchange also said customers could verify that their assets are backed at a minimum ratio of 1:1 through its proof-of-reserves system.
The Oct. 29 attack targeted Binance’s hot wallets across multiple blockchains, with blockchain analytics firm TRM Labs attributing the theft to North Korea’s TraderTraitor group. Following the breach, Binance said it had set aside more than $6.34 billion in company funds to cover the losses.
Thursday’s announcement marks the end of a phased recovery process that began on Nov. 1, when Binance resumed Bitcoin (BTC) withdrawals before gradually restoring services across other blockchain networks.

articles.title: Coinbase Says UK DeFi Rules Shut Out Regulated Crypto Firms
articles.text:
UK is ‘getting it wrong’ on DeFi regulation, says Coinbase
Coinbase and Stand With Crypto argue that the FCA’s proposed DeFi rules could leave UK users without regulated access to decentralized finance.
Coinbase and Stand With Crypto, a crypto advocacy group backed by the exchange, are pushing back against the UK’s proposed approach to decentralized finance (DeFi), arguing that restrictions on regulated crypto platforms could leave consumers with fewer safeguards when accessing DeFi services.
The criticism follows reports on Nov. 26 that the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) plans to proceed with tighter rules and authorization requirements for DeFi platforms, citing money laundering risks exposed by the $6.3 billion Binance hack. Although the attack targeted a centralized exchange, hackers moved stolen funds through decentralized protocols, complicating efforts to trace and freeze the assets.
Katie Harries, head of policy for Europe at Coinbase, said the proposals could limit opportunities for regulated firms to work with authorities on consumer safeguards.
“The UK is getting its approach to DeFi wrong,” Harries told Cointelegraph. “This isn’t a ban on UK consumers using DeFi; it’s a ban on giving them a regulated route to use it.”
In an October opinion piece for Cointelegraph, Harries argued that the proposed framework could effectively prevent regulated crypto platforms from offering DeFi services, as requirements to execute customer orders through authorized trading venues could exclude decentralized protocols with no central operator capable of obtaining FCA authorization.
Related: Japan weighs tighter oversight of DeFi, self-custodial wallets
UK users could face fewer DeFi options
Harries argued that regulated platforms could help address the FCA’s concerns around DeFi through due diligence and safeguards.
The FCA has previously used regulatory sandboxes to allow financial services firms to test new products in live markets under regulatory oversight. On Feb. 25, the regulator named four regulated entities to test out stablecoin products within its regulatory sandbox.
“The UK has got a lot right on crypto, but its approach is closing the door on DeFi innovation,” Harries said.
Harry Pearce-Gould, general manager at Stand With Crypto, argued that the proposals could leave UK users with fewer options for accessing DeFi services. “That leaves UK crypto users without the trusted, regulated routes to access DeFi that will be available to people doing the same thing in other jurisdictions.”
He said people should be able to use crypto for financial activities such as borrowing against their holdings, provided they have clear information about the associated risks.
UK’s ambitions as a global crypto hub
The implications could extend beyond consumer protection, potentially putting the UK at a competitive disadvantage in the digital asset industry, according to Harries. “The UK is creating a prohibition, and that doesn’t sit right with its ambition to be a global centre for digital assets,” she said.
The FCA closed consultations on its proposed DeFi guidance and wider crypto regulatory framework on Nov. 18, with final guidance expected in January 2027. The new regime is scheduled to take effect on Oct. 25, 2027.
Related: Binance says it obtained $6.5B worldwide freezing order after hack

articles.title: Japan’s FSA Explores New Rules for Decentralized Finance
articles.text:
Japan weighs tighter oversight of DeFi, self-custodial wallets
Japan’s financial regulator is exploring measures to curb illicit finance risks, including potential restrictions on access to DeFi services.
Japan’s Financial Services Agency (FSA) is weighing potential new regulations for decentralized finance (DeFi) and self-custodial wallet providers as part of a broader effort to address risks associated with onchain finance.
In a discussion paper dated Thursday, the regulator raised the possibility of discouraging users from accessing DeFi services that lack adequate Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing controls.
The FSA also asked whether regulated businesses that interact with DeFi, including stablecoin issuers, on- and off-ramp providers and financial institutions, should play a role in mitigating illicit finance risks when no party responsible for regulatory compliance can be identified.
The regulator questioned how to identify parties responsible for DeFi services that claim to be decentralized but retain centralized elements, and whether front-end providers that give users access to decentralized exchanges should be subject to financial regulation.
The question of who should be held responsible for DeFi activities remains unresolved in other major markets. The European Union excludes fully decentralized crypto services without intermediaries from its Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation, while US regulators have largely focused on the nature of financial activities and the degree of control exercised by developers or operators. The stalled US CLARITY Act seeks to clarify which DeFi participants should be subject to financial regulation.
Japan weighs safeguards for self-custodial wallets
The FSA noted that direct regulation of self-custodial wallet use and providers that solely develop or sell software or hardware remains uncommon internationally but raised questions about whether additional measures are needed to protect users and prevent illicit financial activity.
Japan already requires domestic virtual asset service providers to collect information and maintain records on transactions involving self-custodial wallets, according to the FSA. Potential anti-fraud measures also include cooling-off periods for transfers from newly opened crypto exchange accounts to self-custodial wallets.
The discussions form part of a broader financial strategy announced by the FSA in July to promote onchain finance, with the initiative’s interim findings targeted for early 2027.

articles.title: Spain Moves to Allow Crypto Account Freezes Over AML Suspicions
articles.text:
Spain moves to grant financial watchdog power to freeze crypto accounts
A new decree would allow Spain’s financial intelligence unit to suspend crypto accounts, with firms facing fines for noncompliance.
A decree published on Nov. 25 would give Spain’s financial intelligence unit, Sepblac, the power to freeze crypto accounts and halt transactions without prior judicial authorization when it suspects money laundering or terrorist financing.
The measures are scheduled to take effect on Jan. 25, 2027. Under Spain’s Constitution, the Congress of Deputies must vote to ratify or repeal the decree within 30 days of its promulgation. If ratified, crypto companies operating in Spain would have to comply with suspension orders or face financial penalties.
According to the decree, Sepblac would be able to suspend the use of a digital asset account or a business relationship for up to five business days, while transactions in progress could be held for up to 10 business days. Although the initial suspension of an account or transaction would be at the discretion of Sepblac, it could be extended by a court at the request of public prosecutors.
Nikolai Timofejev, head of licensing and regulatory affairs at legal consulting firm Prifinance, told Cointelegraph that crypto firms should start preparing for the change before it takes effect. “My advice is to treat it like an operational workstream with a named person who receives Sepblac’s orders,” he said. “Non-compliance amounts to a very serious infringement attracting fines starting at €150,000.”
Firms to act quickly on Sepblac orders
Timofejev explained that crypto companies should be ready to respond quickly, acting on suspension orders the day they receive them to avoid penalties.
The person in charge of responding to Sepblac’s orders should have the authority to “immediately (same day) freeze client withdrawals and transactions.” Companies affected would be responsible for tracking when each order expires.
Firms are also required to report suspicious activity to Sepblac, which, under the decree, would have three business days to issue a transaction suspension order if warranted.
Timofejev expressed support for the decree, saying he hoped “to see similar measures implemented across the entire EU.”
For crypto service providers operating in Spain, the new rules would add another layer of compliance obligations alongside those established under the EU’s Markets in Crypto-Assets Regulation (MiCA).
Related: UK regulator plans tighter DeFi rules, citing $6.3B Binance hack: Report

articles.title: Fed Must Turn Dovish to Avoid Risk-Asset ‘Meltdown,’ Analysis Says
articles.text:
Crypto on notice as hawkish Fed risks December ‘meltdown’
Economist Robin Brooks warned of dire consequences for stocks if the Federal Reserve fails to deliver dovish cues before the FOMC blackout period.
Risk assets could face a “full meltdown” within the next two weeks if the US Federal Reserve maintains its hawkish policy outlook, analysis warns.
Key points:
- The Federal Reserve’s hawkish monetary policy could trigger a “full meltdown” in risk assets before its December interest rate decision, economist Robin Brooks warned.
- WTI crude oil fell to $79.25 per barrel, its lowest level since Aug. 10, while the US Dollar Index (DXY) hit a nine-month high of 104.5 on Monday.
- Market stress could ultimately prompt the Fed to leave interest rates unchanged despite widespread expectations of a 25-basis-point hike.
Risk-asset “full meltdown” puts Fed rate hike in doubt
Economist Robin Brooks, a senior fellow at the Brookings Institution and former chief foreign exchange (FX) strategist at Goldman Sachs, forecast Wednesday that the US central bank could ultimately abandon its widely expected 25-basis-point interest rate hike in December.
Despite falling oil prices and US dollar strength rising, the Fed has maintained a hawkish stance on future policy moves, signaling that interest rates may need to rise and remain elevated.
Last week, Federal Reserve Gov. Christopher Waller said that the central bank may need to “shock” markets with a 50-basis-point rate hike to curb price increases being passed on to consumers by business.
US WTI crude oil fell below $80 per barrel for the first time since Aug. 10 this week.
CFDs on WTI crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
For Brooks, tightening policy amid falling oil markets is an “error” that spells acute pain for stocks and the broader risk-asset cohort by driving up real interest rates. “I’ve been banging the drum that markets are heading for full meltdown because the Fed is hiking into falling oil prices, a policy error that’s giving us a super-charged rise in real rates,” he wrote.
“That’s causing the Dollar to rise sharply versus emerging markets as this particular carry trade unwinds in chaotic fashion.”
On Nov. 28, the second Saturday preceding the Dec. 8-9 meeting of the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC), at which a decision on monetary policy, including the federal funds rate, will be announced, the Fed’s “blackout” period begins. During blackouts, FOMC participants cannot give interviews or otherwise speak in public on monetary policy and macroeconomic developments.
Brooks argues that without efforts to calm markets before the blackout period, selling pressure on risk assets could intensify.
“That’ll bring a full meltdown in markets and we’ll end up not getting a hike on December 9. Unfortunately, this is the path we’re on,” he continued.
Markets see negligible chance of surprise hike pause
The upheaval intensified on Monday, as the US Dollar Index - a measure of the dollar’s strength against a basket of major currencies - hit 104.5, its highest level since March. It has remained above 100 since mid-September.
US Dollar Index one-week chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
At the same time, US stock markets continue to deal with compounding sell-side pressure. On Friday, the S&P 500 fell to 6,882 points, a level last seen in mid-April.
Brooks noted that even Nvidia’s reinstatement of CEO Jensen Huang failed to lift investor sentiment. Beyond stocks, meanwhile, gold saw its worst 60-day sell-off in over 40 years.
“It seems increasingly likely that we go into this without a dovish pivot, in which case the wheels might really start coming off in markets,” he concluded.
“If that’s where we’re headed, we might well end up with no hike on December 9 as markets go full meltdown.”
The latest data from CME FedWatch shows that markets still overwhelmingly expect a 25-basis-point rate hike in December. As of Thursday, the probability of the Fed keeping its target rate unchanged at 3.75% to 4% stood at just 0.5%.
Fed target-rate probabilities for Dec. 8-9 FOMC meeting. Source: CME Group

articles.title: Stablecoin Critic Poised to Take Helm of European Central Bank
articles.text:
BIS chief Pablo Hernández de Cos set to become next ECB president: FT
The Spanish economist has questioned the viability of stablecoins for widespread payments while backing the development of a digital euro.
Pablo Hernández de Cos, general manager of the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) and a critic of stablecoins, is set to succeed Christine Lagarde as president of the European Central Bank (ECB) after securing the backing of a majority of eurozone governments, the Financial Times reported Thursday, citing people familiar with the matter.
Hernández de Cos, a former governor of Spain’s central bank, is expected to replace Lagarde on Feb. 7 after the Dutch government withdrew its support for rival candidate Klaas Knot, a former governor of the Dutch central bank. The appointment remains subject to formal approval.
Speaking at the Jackson Hole Economic Symposium in August, Hernández de Cos argued that stablecoins in their current form were not a credible means of payment at scale, favoring tokenized bank deposits for everyday payments and wholesale settlement.
While acknowledging some specialized uses for stablecoins, he warned that widespread adoption of US dollar-backed stablecoins abroad could undermine monetary sovereignty and weaken domestic monetary policy transmission, while a shift away from bank deposits could increase bank funding costs.
Hernández de Cos has been more receptive to central bank digital currencies. In a 2023 speech, he said that a digital euro could promote innovation in payments and safeguard Europe’s monetary sovereignty.
He is now poised to lead the ECB as it advances its digital euro project, with a pilot planned for 2027 and a potential launch in 2029, subject to legislative approval.

articles.title: Vibecoded GTA 6 PC Ports Are Now Rendering In-Game Graphics Despite Take-Two Crackdown
articles.text:
In brief
- Unofficial GTA 6 PC ports are now rendering characters, environments, textures, and even ray-traced lighting.
- Some developers report achieving around 20 frames per second, just days after obtaining the game's executable file.
- Development continues despite Take-Two's copyright takedown campaign against 3,007 GitHub repositories.
It took Rockstar Games more than a decade to develop Grand Theft Auto 6. It took a bunch of anonymous vibe coders less than a week to get parts of it running on a platform Rockstar hasn't released it for.
Unofficial PC ports of GTA 6 are now capable of rendering in-game graphics and handling player inputs, according to footage circulating on social media. Some projects have achieved speeds of around 20 frames per second, despite the increasingly aggressive efforts of Rockstar parent company Take-Two Interactive to shut them down.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
A developer going by AvatarManz reportedly achieved between six and 20 frames per second using an AMD Radeon RX 7900 XTX, a high-end graphics card. The unofficial port consumed up to 46 GB of system memory, considerably more than what a typical gaming PC has available.
Another demonstration reported Thursday appears to show a character riding a jet ski and driving along the coast at between 19 and 23 frames per second. Performance drops to around 12 frames per second in urban areas, and patches of water are visibly missing from the scene.
new GTA 6 PC gameplay shows walking around the prologue, with textures, lighting and physics looking much better. Ray tracing is reportedly working too.
Still only 1–3fps on an RTX 5070 Ti, Ryzen 7 7800X3D and 32GB DDR5. Visuals are coming along, performance has a way to go. pic.twitter.com/ON00pzHFHX
— Brackz (@Brackzmeta) November 25, 2026
According to community tracking data site Portwatch VI, at least six of 35 tracked projects have reportedly reached interactive gameplay. Some developers have also managed to get ray tracing working, a computationally demanding technique that simulates how light interacts with objects.
The footage and performance figures have not been independently verified, and none of the projects has demonstrated that the entire game can be played reliably on a PC.
How AI is accelerating the GTA 6 PC port
Much of the progress comes from developers relying on vibe coding, a method of software development in which users instruct AI models to generate and debug code using natural language rather than manually writing every instruction.
The developers aren't recreating GTA 6 from scratch. They're reverse-engineering an existing Xbox build and developing software that allows its code to execute on Windows, translating console-specific instructions and accommodating differences in how PCs handle graphics and other hardware functions.
AI coding tools such as Anthropic's Claude have dramatically accelerated this kind of work, reducing some tasks that previously took months to days. Optimizing the resulting software and fixing the inevitable bugs are separate challenges, especially for a game as complex as GTA 6.
#1 Searched Person on Google 2026?
And the whole thing, of course, spaked a meme coin.
As Decrypt previously reported, notorious Rockstar leaker Cyberleek distributed what they claimed was a 209 GB Xbox build of GTA 6, withholding its main executable file as part of an attempt to push their CYBERLEEK meme coin to a $15 million market capitalization.
The token failed to reach its target, but Cyberleek released the executable on November 23 anyway. Within a day, some of the most prominent porting projects, including Leonida and GTA6Modding, went dark.
Take-Two subsequently confirmed its involvement through a copyright complaint targeting Leonida. GitHub disabled 3,007 repositories associated with the project.
In its DMCA notice, Take-Two argued that the project reproduces copyrighted material and violates Rockstar's terms of service, which prohibit unauthorized reverse engineering and decompilation.
Some developers have since taken their work into private communities, making their progress harder to independently assess.
Rockstar released GTA 6 on November 19 for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X and S, targeting 30 frames per second on consoles. It has yet to announce a release date for an official PC version.

articles.title: How EU Crypto Sanctions Could Cut Off Kyrgyz Exchanges
articles.text:
How EU brokers could lose access to Kyrgyz crypto exchanges
A vote on Kyrgyzstan could make an exchange’s home country the deciding factor in whether a European broker can use it to settle a trade.
A European Union sanctions list published in July has an empty annex for more countries, and Kyrgyzstan could be its first entry.
When authorities disrupted the Russian crypto exchange Garantex in March 2025, its employees set up Grinex, an exchange registered in Kyrgyzstan, and moved customer deposits there, according to the US Treasury. British sanctions officials later traced substantial transfers between Grinex and licensed international exchanges.
That episode may help explain why EU brokers may soon need to check where an exchange is based before placing a trade. In July, the EU gave itself the power to bar its operators from dealing, directly or indirectly, with crypto providers established in a country that systematically and persistently fails to prevent sanctions evasion through crypto services.
Related: Binance lists som-pegged stablecoin as Kyrgyzstan deepens crypto push
The EU left the country list, Annex LVII, empty. Kyrgyzstan is the proposed first entry, the Kyiv Independent reported.
As of Nov. 26, the proposal still needed unanimous approval from the EU’s 27 member states. If it passes, a European broker could check the name of a longtime settlement partner, find no sanctions listing for the firm, and still have to take its next trade elsewhere.

articles.title: What Is Self-Custody? How to Hold Your Own Crypto Keys
articles.text:
In brief
- Self-custody means holding the private keys to your own crypto, rather than leaving them with an exchange or other third party.
- It removes the risk of a custodian failing or freezing your funds, but makes you solely responsible for keeping your keys safe.
- Self-custody options range from software wallets on a phone to hardware, air-gapped and multi-signature setups, each with different tradeoffs.
When you buy crypto on an exchange, the exchange usually holds it for you. Your account shows a balance, but the private keys that control the coins belong to the trading platform.
The risk is that if an exchange collapses, is hacked or freezes withdrawals, its customers can lose access to their funds. The collapse of FTX in November 2022 left millions of users unable to withdraw, and turned the old crypto saying "not your keys, not your coins" into a rallying cry.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Self-custody is the alternative: holding your crypto yourself, with no intermediary standing between you and your money. This guide explains what self-custody is, how it works, the tools available and the risks it brings.
What is self-custody?
Self-custody means you, and only you, control the private keys to your crypto.
On a blockchain, coins are not stored in a wallet in the way cash sits in a purse. They are recorded on a public ledger, and a private key, a long secret number, is what proves you have the right to spend them. Whoever holds the private key controls the coins.
With a custodial service, such as a centralized exchange, the company holds the keys on your behalf, and you rely on it to process your withdrawals. With a self-custodial, or non-custodial, wallet, the keys are generated and stored on your own device, and transactions only happen when you approve them.
How does self-custody work?
When you set up a self-custodial wallet, it generates a seed phrase, usually a list of 12 or 24 words. The seed phrase is a human-readable backup of your private keys: anyone who has it can recreate your wallet on another device and move your funds.
That makes the seed phrase the single most important thing to protect. Most guides recommend writing it down on paper or stamping it into metal, storing it somewhere safe offline, and never typing it into a website, sharing it or saving it in a photo or cloud file.
Self-custodial wallets come in several forms:
- 📱 Software wallets are apps on a phone, computer or browser, such as MetaMask. They are free and convenient, but because they run on internet-connected devices, they are sometimes called "hot" wallets.
- 🔐 Hardware wallets are small devices that keep private keys offline and sign transactions internally, so the keys never touch your computer. They are a common form of "cold storage."
- ✈️ Air-gapped wallets go a step further, never connecting to the internet, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth or even a USB cable. Transactions are passed back and forth using microSD cards or QR codes.
- 🗝️ Multi-signature wallets require more than one key to approve a transaction, such as two of three keys. That means a single lost or stolen key isn't enough to lose your funds.
Custodial vs. self-custody
Custodial services are easier to use. If you forget your password, you can reset it, and an exchange handles the security of its own systems. But you are trusting the company to stay solvent, keep your funds safe and let you withdraw when you want to.
Self-custody removes that counterparty risk, and means no company can freeze your funds or block a transaction. The tradeoff is responsibility: there is no password reset. If you lose your seed phrase, or someone steals it, there is usually no way to get your crypto back.
Did you know?
Welshman James Howells says the keys to about 8,000 BTC are on a hard drive that was thrown out in 2013 and buried in a landfill in Newport, Wales.
The risks of self-custody
Losing your keys is the most common risk, but not the only one.
Hardware can have flaws. In July 2026, a firmware vulnerability in Coldcard, a Bitcoin-only air-gapped hardware wallet, let attackers reconstruct some users' seed phrases. Losses rose to nearly $114 million in Bitcoin within days, according to Galaxy Research. Even the most secure devices depend on their makers getting the code right.
Phishing and malware are a constant threat to software wallets, and scammers often pose as wallet support staff to trick users into handing over seed phrases.
Holders also face physical danger. So-called "wrench attacks," in which criminals use violence to force victims to hand over crypto, have surged. Blockchain security firm CertiK verified 52 wrench attacks worldwide in the first half of 2026, up from 39 a year earlier, and Chainalysis said such attacks were on pace for a record year.
The threat is one reason holders have pushed back against proposals to make them report large self-custody holdings to tax authorities, warning that such records could leak.
How to move your crypto into self-custody
Moving crypto off an exchange generally involves a few steps:
- Choose a wallet that supports the assets you hold, whether a software wallet, a hardware wallet or a combination.
- Set it up and back up your seed phrase offline before you put any money in.
- Copy your receiving address from the wallet. Check it carefully, since crypto sent to the wrong address usually can't be recovered.
- Send a small test transaction from the exchange first, and confirm it arrives.
- Withdraw the rest once the test has worked, making sure you select the right blockchain network.
Self-custody and regulation
Regulators have long debated how to handle self-custodial, or "unhosted," wallets. In October 2026, the U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network withdrew a 2020 proposal that would have required banks and money services businesses to keep records on transactions with self-custodial wallets over $3,000 and report those over $10,000.
In France, the Senate rejected a plan in November 2026 that would have required holders to declare self-custodied crypto worth more than €100,000.
The future of self-custody
Self-custody is starting to extend beyond humans. In 2026, MetaMask launched Agent Wallet, a self-custodial wallet that lets AI agents execute on-chain trades within limits set by the user, while Coinbase introduced its own self-custodial wallets for AI agents.
Wallet makers are also working to make self-custody easier for newcomers, with features such as social logins and passkeys that reduce reliance on seed phrases. But the core principle remains the same: whoever controls the keys controls the crypto.

articles.title: Nasdaq Exec Pushes for Common EU Rules on Tokenized Securities
articles.text:
Nasdaq exec pushes for common EU rules on tokenized securities
Nasdaq’s Roland Chai backed exploring common EU rules for tokenized securities and said its Swedish subsidiary had applied for a DLT license.
Roland Chai, executive vice president and head of digital liquidity networks at Nasdaq, urged European Union lawmakers to explore creating a dedicated legal framework for tokenized securities to avoid legal uncertainties arising from fragmented regulations.
“We do see merit in exploring a 28th regime for dedicated, harmonized EU-level framework for tokenized securities issuance,” Chai said, speaking at the European Commission’s tokenization roundtable in Brussels on Thursday.
The term “28th regime” refers to the concept of an optional EU-wide set of rules that would apply alongside the national systems of the bloc’s 27 member states.
Chai said that Nasdaq’s Swedish subsidiary had applied for its first distributed ledger technology (DLT) trading and settlement license. Nasdaq was also considering accepting tokenized collateral, but faced constraints under current EU rules.
Chai’s comments echo a recent warning from European Central Bank President Christine Lagarde, who said Friday that Europe risks developing a fragmented tokenized securities market unless it establishes common standards. Without them, trading platforms could be unable to settle transactions with one another.
Related: Swiss central bank, UBS and SIX study ledger for tokenized settlement
BlackRock points to institutional demand for tokenized funds
BlackRock’s head of digital cash Hannah Winter said institutional clients seeking access to regulated money market funds were driving demand for tokenization.
“For us it’s absolutely demand-driven,” Winter said at the roundtable. “The ability to leverage a tokenized money market fund increases the return on those balances, but also frees up the ability for operations to be unlocked on a 24/7 basis.”
Winter said the primary uses of tokenized funds include treasury and liquidity management, as well as collateral for derivatives positions.
In August, BlackRock announced plans to offer tokenized versions of select European money market funds using JPMorgan’s blockchain infrastructure, including pound sterling, euro and US dollar share classes from BlackRock’s Institutional Cash Series.
BlackRock’s BUIDL fund, total assets under management and monthly returns. Source: RWA.xyz
BlackRock launched its first tokenized US dollar-denominated institutional liquidity fund, BUIDL, in March 2024. The fund had $1.55 billion in assets, down nearly 30% over the past 30 days, and a trailing one-year return of 3.59%, according to RWA.xyz.

articles.title: Before the Sell-Off, AI Stocks Showed Dot-Com-Level Bubble Signals: Study
articles.text:
In brief
- Researchers from London Business School and the University of Cambridge put the probability of an AI stock market bubble in September as high as 97%.
- The study used artificial intelligence to analyze nearly 800,000 articles from The Economist and examined 22 historical financial bubbles.
- The researchers found that unusually intense media warnings can predict weaker market returns, despite the financial press routinely overestimating crash risks.
Researchers from London Business School and the University of Cambridge have estimated that there was as much as a 97% probability that AI-related stocks were in a financial bubble in September, before the recent sell-off wiped trillions of dollars off technology stocks.
The findings, highlighted Wednesday by London Business School, come from an analysis of 170 years of financial journalism. The researchers used artificial intelligence to determine whether the language journalists use to describe financial markets can help identify speculative bubbles before they burst.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short ANT with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
September's readings were comparable to or higher than those recorded at the peak of the dot-com bubble in March 2000, after which the Nasdaq lost roughly 77% of its value.
The research, titled Crying Wolf, was conducted by London Business School finance professor Marco Grotteria and Cambridge researchers Afonso Monteiro and Constantine Yannelis.
The team analyzed 795,964 articles published by The Economist between 1843 and 2013, identifying approximately 486,000 relevant to financial markets. They subsequently extended their index through September 2026.
Instead of simply counting how many times journalists mentioned the word "bubble," the researchers used large language models to identify language associated with excessive speculation, concerns about asset valuations, regulatory warnings, and investor euphoria. They then compared their monthly readings against 22 documented financial bubbles across 10 countries.
When the financial press cries wolf
One of the more interesting findings was just how frequently financial journalists get it wrong. Historically, their coverage implied an average 20% probability of a major market crash within six months, compared with an actual frequency of just 5.7%.
What proved useful was measuring how much more concerned journalists became relative to their usual coverage. In 74% of comparisons between months during financial bubbles and ordinary months, the researchers' index registered a higher reading during the bubble, rising to 94% for the dot-com episode.
But the widely cited 97% figure represents the most pessimistic of the researchers' estimates. Two alternative calculations put the probability at approximately 40%.
The index also proved useful in forecasting stock market performance. When tested against data outside its estimation sample, it reduced the average squared error of 12-month Nasdaq return forecasts by 11% compared with predictions based on historical average returns.
AI can succeed even if its investors don't
Nvidia shares had fallen approximately 48% from their peak by last week, while the Nasdaq is trading well below its October record, prompting some analysts to raise concerns of a bubble.
Owen Lamont, a portfolio manager at Acadian Asset Management and former University of Chicago finance professor who previously expressed skepticism about the existence of an AI bubble, has also revised his assessment, recently assigning a 70% probability to the U.S. stock market being in one.
The researchers distinguish between the economic potential of artificial intelligence and the amount of money investors expect to make from it. The internet fundamentally changed the global economy, for example, even though many of the companies that attracted enormous investments during the dot-com boom never survived its collapse.
"The technology may be very productive, but investors are still learning what it is worth," Marco Grotteria, one of the researchers said.
The study also found that central banks and regulators could reduce their expected losses by between 20% and 33% by incorporating the index into their decisions, provided they consider failing to identify a bubble substantially more damaging than issuing a false alarm.
For policymakers who assign equal costs to both mistakes, the researchers found no benefit from using the index.

articles.title: 7 Bizarre Things Crypto Whales Spent A Fortune On
articles.text:
7 bizarre things crypto whales spent a fortune on
The crypto rich have spent their fortunes on everything from dinosaur skeletons to rotting fruit, with some purchases defying belief.
They say a fool and his money are soon parted, but perhaps the idiom should be extended to crypto multi-millionaires and billionaires, who get their kicks from spending their fortunes on some truly bizarre things.
From a trip to space funded with Bitcoin to a $69 million nonfungible token, check out the seven weirdest ways crypto fortunes have been allocated so far.
1. A trip to space that never took off
For some early Bitcoin adopters, the ultimate luxury purchase wasn’t a Lambo or a Malibu mansion; it was a ticket off the planet.
In November 2013, British entrepreneur and Virgin Group founder Richard Branson announced that Virgin Galactic would accept BTC for spaceflight tickets.
At $250,000 a pop, the announcement piqued the interest of some of crypto’s earliest investors. In March 2014, Gemini co-founders Cameron and Tyler Winklevoss each purchased a ticket using Bitcoin to fund the space plunge — which they never actually took.
Bitcoin, space and beyond. Source: Winklevoss Capital
After stumping up 312.5 BTC each, the flights were repeatedly delayed until the Virgin Galactic VSS Unity was officially retired from spaceflight in June 2024.
Tron founder Justin Sun did make it into space briefly on Blue Origin in 2025 for $28 million, while f2pool co-founder Chun Wang actually commanded SpaceX’s Fram2 mission.
It was the first human spaceflight to fly over both poles of the earth. It’s not known how much he paid for the privilege but estimates suggest the four person mission would cost around $220 million.
2. A $6.2 million banana
Everyone’s heard of Bitcoin Pizza Day, when developer Laszlo Hanyecz infamously spent 10,000 BTC on two pizzas, but Bitcoin Banana Day gets considerably less attention.
Yet few examples capture the intersection of crypto and wealth quite like Justin Sun’s outrageous spend on, well, a banana.
Related: Pudgy Penguins expands retail footprint with Target trading card rollout
In November 2024, the founder of Tron paid $6.24 million for Italian artist Maurizio Cattelan’s Comedian, which consists of a banana duct-taped to a wall.
Sun subsequently followed through on a promise to eat the artwork, holding a press conference in Hong Kong where he took a bite out of the yellow fruit. If it were anyone else it might have been a Dada-esque artistic statement about the transience of worth in a consumption-based society, but it was Justin Sun, so it was probably just a publicity stunt.
Top banana. Source: Sothebys
He could have just gone to the 7-Eleven down the street and scored a banana for $1.50, but then he wouldn’t have been able to attract so much attention by eating it. The actual work he bought wasn’t the banana or duct tape, it was a certificate of authenticity for instructions on how to tape the banana to a wall.
3. A chance to come back from the dead
Some people spend their fortunes trying to live more comfortably; others are more interested in the chance to live again.
Hal Finney, one of Bitcoin’s earliest contributors and the recipient of the first Bitcoin transaction from Satoshi Nakamoto, was cryopreserved after his death in August 2014.
Finney was a member of the Alcor Life Extension Foundation for more than two decades, and after his death, his body was preserved in the hopes that future medical technology might one day make revival possible.
Even better? Finney’s cryopreservation was paid for through a combination of life insurance and Bitcoin donated by fans. Crypto investor Peter Theil and “Bitcoin Jesus” Roger Ver are also set to undergo the process. Ver told Magazine back in 2021 he’d actually seriously considered killing himself and being cryptopreserved to be revived later, to avoid being sent to jail as a 23-year old.
4. A skeleton of a Triceratops
Some collectors want paintings on their walls, others want bananas, and others still want something that has been dead for 69 million years.
In 2025, a group of investors, including Yoann Turpin, co-founder of cryptocurrency market maker Wintermute, spent $5 million on a dinosaur skeleton.
Yoann Turpin spent $5 million on a dinosaur skeleton. Source: Bloomberg
The Triceratops fossil is one of only two dozen or so known specimens, and was shipped from Wyoming to Turpin’s storage facility in Singapore.
Beyond the obvious novelty value, he reportedly said its appeal includes the fossil’s scarcity, which he likened to Bitcoin’s limited supply. One dino-skeleton will always equal one dino-skeleton.
5. A $1.5 million Titanic survivor’s watch
From one enthusiastic collector of old relics to another. Patrick Gruhn, former head of FTX Europe, spent a chunk of his crypto fortune on a gold pocket watch recovered from the body of John Jacob Astor IV, the wealthiest passenger aboard the Titanic.
Related: 10 weirdest things ever tokenized... including farts
Gruhn spent $1.5 million at auction in 2024 and reportedly bought the old timepiece as a gift for his wife, partly because of his fascination with the Astor family’s history, and perhaps partly due to an affinity for sinking ships.
6. The world’s largest black diamond
HEX founder Richard Heart’s taste in luxury goods could hardly be called understated.
In February 2022, he acquired The Enigma, a 555.55-carat black diamond, for approximately $4.3 million.
The enormous stone, also known as a carbonado diamond, is one of the largest faceted diamonds ever offered at auction, and the theories of its origins stretch from deep inside the Earth’s core to outer space.
Richard Heart bought a 555.55-carat black diamond. Source: Rapaport
Heart later renamed it the HEX.com diamond, connecting the unusual purchase to his cryptocurrency project. The US Securities and Exchange Commission launched a civil case in 2023 alleging that he misappropriated investor assets, including funds used to purchase the diamond. Heart was arrested in Turkey earlier this year due to an Interpol Red Notice connected to separate Finnish tax fraud charges.
7. A $69 million NFT
What to buy for the person who has it all?
A $69 million NFT, perhaps. That’s what cryptocurrency investor MetaKovan paid in March 2021 for EVERYDAYS: THE FIRST 5000 DAYS, a digital collage by artist Beeple of 5,000 images created over 13 years.
At 42,329.453 Ether, the sale made it not only the most expensive NFT ever sold at the time, but also one of the most expensive artworks by a living artist.
The owner has no intention of selling the work, but it seems unlikely to fetch a similar price today. But he has purchased himself a notable place in art and crypto history.
Magazine: AI agents are using credit cards. Where does that leave crypto?

articles.title: Vitalik Buterin Calls for Verifiable Chips as Hardware Wallet Threats Evolve
articles.text:
Vitalik Buterin calls for verifiable chips as hardware wallet threats evolve
Buterin warned that future attacks could use lookalike chips with hidden malicious functions, making hardware tampering harder to detect.
Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin on Thursday called for enhanced verifiability in computer chips, citing evolving security threats in the hardware wallet sector.
Buterin said in a blog post that most commercial open-source chips do not disclose enough detail to verify their physical construction. Publishing what a chip is programmed to do is different from providing a blueprint against which inspectors can check the hardware itself.
“This concern is not just theoretical,” Buterin said, adding that the crypto industry has seen attacks that involve inserting spy implants into hardware wallets before they get sold to consumers.
Buterin warned that future attacks could be harder to detect, with malicious functions built into replacement chips that resemble legitimate ones.
“This, you cannot detect with the naked eye,” he wrote.
In October, Ledger said malicious implants in devices sold through reseller CryptoBilis captured recovery phrases and transmitted them over cellular networks. Ledger suspended reseller sales in Southeast Asia and Hong Kong, tightened distribution rules and offered X-ray inspections after tampered devices surfaced beyond the region.
Trezor in November said it found similar implants in three devices sold through the same reseller. The company released a firmware update to stop the implants from capturing data and reduced its reseller network by about 80%.
Related: Ledger’s early implant warnings deserved more action, Karpelès says
Buterin envisions a split between performance and security
Buterin warned that inspecting chips would remain a specialist task for professional auditors, journalists and civil society groups, even if hardware designs became fully open-source.
“In order for computation to be democratized, the hardware layer must be open for participation and tinkering too,” he wrote.
Still, Buterin said that given extreme commercial pressures that companies face, the industry cannot expect all hardware to become open source.
He said he hoped the industry would split into performance hardware and secure hardware. While secure hardware might be “10x less efficient or more,” it would still be sufficient for most everyday applications.
Magazine: Scammer loses $4.8M stored on tampered Ledgers: Asia Express

articles.title: Bitcoin Holds Above $60K as Death Cross Clouds Thanksgiving Recovery
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitcoin rose 1.36% over 24 hours to $60,392 but remained down nearly 4% over the past week.
- Bitcoin’s 50-day EMA has crossed below its 200-day EMA, while the S&P 500 remains in golden cross territory.
- U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs have recorded roughly $5.39 billion in November outflows, ahead of Friday’s $7 billion Bitcoin options expiry.
Bitcoin and most major cryptocurrencies edged slightly higher Thursday as U.S. stock exchanges closed for Thanksgiving, a day after inflation data and fresh tariff concerns rattled markets.
Bitcoin traded at around $60,560 as of just after 1:00 p.m. ET, up 1.39% over the past 24 hours but down 3.67% over the past week, according to Decrypt's price tracker. The largest cryptocurrency has recovered roughly 5% from Wednesday’s low of $57,500.
Ethereum gained 0.87% to just under $1,700, while XRP and Solana rose 3.1% and 2.17%, respectively.
The Nasdaq Composite recovered from an intraday plunge of as much as 4.6% Wednesday to close down 0.62%. The S&P 500 contract for difference (CFD), a derivative tracking the index, was up 0.67% on Thursday at around 7,226 points, per TradingView. The cash index itself was not trading.
Wednesday’s selloff followed a combination of stronger-than-expected U.S. economic growth, proposed tariffs and renewed concerns over AI stocks, as Decrypt previously reported. The Federal Reserve’s preferred measure of inflation, the Personal Consumption Expenditures price index, rose 3.8% year over year in October, complicating efforts to bring inflation back to its 2% target.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Bitcoin in death cross as stocks struggle
Bitcoin’s daily chart looks considerably weaker than its stock market counterpart. Its 50-day exponential moving average (EMA) has crossed below its 200-day EMA, forming a bearish signal known as a death cross. EMAs track average prices over a given period, assigning more weight to recent trading activity.
Both averages are trending lower, with Bitcoin trading roughly 16% below its 50-day EMA of $71,478 and 19% below its 200-day EMA of $74,516, according to TradingView charts.
The S&P 500 CFD, by contrast, remains in golden cross territory, with its 50-day EMA of 7,517 still above its 200-day EMA of 7,372. The price is below both indicators, however, and the gap between them is narrowing, suggesting the longer-term bullish trend is weakening.
Neither crossover guarantees where prices will go next, but the comparison shows how much more technical damage Bitcoin has sustained. Bitcoin faces potential resistance between $62,000 and $64,000, while recent lows around $57,500 to $58,500 form a possible support zone, followed by November’s low near $55,000.
Around $7 billion worth of Bitcoin options are due to expire Friday on Deribit, with traders favoring contracts that provide protection against price declines more heavily than they did in October. U.S. stock trading will resume Friday, but the NYSE will close early at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Spain Lets Its Financial Intelligence Unit Freeze Crypto Accounts Without a Court Order
articles.text:
In brief
- Spain's financial intelligence unit, Sepblac, can now suspend crypto, bank and payment accounts it suspects are linked to money laundering or terrorist financing.
- Account suspensions can last up to five working days and transaction suspensions up to 10, after which a court must ratify or extend them.
- Previously, Sepblac could only suspend transactions at the request of foreign intelligence units. The government cited the speed of digital transfers and FATF standards.
Spain's financial intelligence unit will be able to freeze crypto accounts it suspects are linked to money laundering or terrorist financing on its own authority, under a royal decree-law published in the country's official gazette on Wednesday.
The measure is tucked into a sweeping decree on consumer credit, which also caps interest rates on consumer loans and regulates buyers of bad loans. It adds a new article to Spain's 2010 anti-money laundering law, allowing the Executive Service of the Commission for the Prevention of Money Laundering and Monetary Offenses, known as Sepblac, to suspend or block a transaction in progress, or suspend the use of a bank, payment or crypto-asset account or a business relationship.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Sepblac can act when it finds indications that the funds could be linked to money laundering or terrorist financing, in order to preserve them while it analyzes the case and, if its suspicions are confirmed, passes the information to the relevant authorities.
Time limits
Suspensions of transactions can last no more than 10 working days, and suspensions of accounts or business relationships no more than five. When a suspicion stems from a suspicious activity report filed by a bank or other firm, Sepblac must order the suspension within three working days. Any suspension must be lifted earlier if it is no longer needed.
After those deadlines, a suspension ends unless a court ratifies or extends it at the request of the public prosecutor's office.
BTC price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
Until now, Sepblac could only suspend transactions at the request of financial intelligence units in other countries. Under the new rules, it can also act on its own analysis or at the request of Spanish police. Firms that fail to comply with a suspension order commit an offense under the money laundering law, while those that comply, and Sepblac itself, are protected from liability.
The government said the change brings Spain in line with standards set by the Financial Action Task Force (FATF), and transposes part of the EU's sixth anti-money laundering directive. The speed of financial transactions, particularly online, allows funds of possible criminal origin to be moved before authorities can finish their analysis, it said.
Crypto in focus
Sepblac handled 204 requests from other EU intelligence units to suspend transactions in 2025, more than double the 90 it received in 2023 and up from 175 in 2024, according to its latest annual report. The amounts involved fell to about €32 million ($35 million) from €92 million ($101 million), and the number of bank accounts affected slipped to 307 from 316.
Suspicious activity reports from crypto service providers rose to 1,672 in 2025, from 972 in 2024. Sepblac said those reports continued to reveal weaknesses in how crypto firms identify the parties to transactions, and named crypto, along with cash, as a key vulnerability, because of its pseudonymity and speed.
The new powers arrive as Spain prepares for its next FATF evaluation, with an on-site visit by assessors scheduled for February 2027 and a plenary discussion in October 2027, according to the watchdog's calendar. The FATF has flagged peer-to-peer stablecoin transfers as a top money laundering risk, and said centralized elements frequently persist in DeFi. In the UK, a taskforce convened by think tank RUSI has warned that crypto laundering is a material risk ahead of its own FATF review.
Other European countries are also expanding their powers over crypto. In Germany, lawmakers have backed giving customs officials powers to seize crypto and other assets of unclear origin.
The decree takes effect two months after publication. As a royal decree-law, it must also be ratified by Spain's Congress of Deputies within 30 days.

articles.title: Standard Chartered’s Zodia Custody Suffers Data Breach
articles.text:
Standard Chartered’s Zodia Custody suffers data breach
Zodia Custody’s CEO said the breach exposed names and email addresses of some clients and employees and was detected by the company Monday.
Update (Nov. 26, 1 p.m. UTC): This article has been updated with Zodia Custody’s statement clarifying the incident’s timeline, the information accessed and its finding of no unauthorized transactions to date.
Standard Chartered’s cryptocurrency custody unit, Zodia Custody suffered a security breach that exposed some client and employee information.
Zodia detected attempts to probe its platform Monday and temporarily took its business-to-business API offline as a precaution, CEO Richard Clark said in a statement Thursday. The company restored the service after implementing additional security measures.
On Tuesday, monitoring revealed that an unauthorized party had accessed publicly available organization details and business contact names and email addresses for a small number of clients and employees.
Zodia’s investigation found no unauthorized transactions.
Cointelegraph approached Standard Chartered and Zodia Custody for comment but didn’t receive an immediate response.
The breach comes just over a month after Standard Chartered signed definitive agreements to acquire Zodia Custody’s regulated operating entities and fold its crypto custody business into the bank’s existing Securities Services operations.
Standard Chartered reportedly began considering incorporating Zodia’s crypto custody business in April. The UK-based lender also expanded its crypto services in September, when Standard Chartered launched spot Bitcoin (BTC) and Ether (ETH) trading for institutional clients in the United Arab Emirates.
