articles.title: OpenAI Fixes ChatGPT Billing Error, Promises to Make it 40% Worse
articles.text:
In brief
- OpenAI corrected a billing error that inadvertently discounted usage of its GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models for most users.
- Subscribers will now reach their usage limits 40% faster on Astra and 25% faster on Sol compared with last week.
- The correction comes as OpenAI prepares to merge ChatGPT's conversational and agentic usage allowances, raising concerns among paying customers.
Have you been particularly happy with how much you've been getting out of your ChatGPT subscription lately? Turns out that was a bug.
OpenAI acknowledged Thursday that a billing error at the launch of its GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol models gave most subscribers more AI usage than the company intended. It has since fixed the mistake, meaning customers will now get less work done for the same monthly fee compared with last week.
“We made a billing mistake at launch of GPT-6.2 that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most users,” OpenAI's Thibault Sottiaux tweeted. “We’ve fixed this now, so the same work will use more of your plan’s usage allowance.”
We made a billing mistake at launch of GPT-6.2 that incorrectly discounted GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol usage for most users.
We’ve fixed this now, so the same work will use more of your plan’s usage allowance. Comparing to last week, you will reach your limits 40% faster on GPT-6.2…
— Tibo (@thsottiaux) November 26, 2026
And it’s not a small bug; in fact, the difference is substantial. Sottiaux said users will reach their limits 40% faster when using GPT-6.2 Astra, OpenAI's most capable model for professional tasks, and 25% faster when using its more economical sibling, GPT-6.2 Sol.
To put that into perspective, if a particular amount of work consumed 50% of your allowance last week, it would consume 70% or more today on Astra, assuming those percentages refer to the rate of consumption.
If a user was running a complex task on extra high or Ultra thinking levels, it may now deplete the whole quota before producing an actual output depending on the instruction.
OpenAI introduced both models on November 17, specifically touting their improved efficiency as a selling point. The company said the models could deliver better results while generating fewer tokens—the small units of information AI models process and produce—allowing subscribers to accomplish more within their existing limits.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short BTC with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
Sottiaux maintains that both models should still offer more effective usage than their respective predecessors. The comparison, however, is now considerably less flattering than it was nine days ago.
OpenAI won't retroactively charge customers for the difference, and other models remain unaffected.
“As a small token to apologize for the mistake, we’ll be adding one banked reset for everyone on Go, Plus, Pro, and Business,” Sottiaux said.
Pun intended, presumably.
ChatGPT's increasingly complicated usage limits
The billing correction comes at a particularly awkward time for OpenAI. As Decrypt reported Wednesday, the company has begun merging ChatGPT's conversational and Work experiences, a change that has prompted complaints from some of its highest-paying subscribers because Chat has huge usage quotas and Work is pretty limited in terms of usage.
Hi. We’re beginning to roll out the combined Chat and Work experience to a small group of Pro users to learn from feedback before we roll out more broadly.
Let us know what you think and where we can improve!
— Tibo (@thsottiaux) November 24, 2026
Ultimately, it may end up cutting the overall usage allocation considerably.
Starting in December, advanced conversations and resource-intensive agentic tasks, such as building software or conducting extensive research, will draw from a shared usage allowance for Plus, Pro, and Business subscribers.
The company hasn't disclosed how large those combined budgets will be, making it difficult to quantify the cumulative effect of the two changes. Thursday's billing correction is separate from the merger.
OpenAI didn’t reply to a request for comments by Decrypt to clarify if both quotas would be added, or the new total allocation will be less than the combined usage people can enjoy today.
Still, subscribers who bought or upgraded their subscriptions after experiencing GPT-6.2's apparent efficiency last week now have a different product in economic terms, even if the models themselves haven't changed.
The banked reset can be redeemed through the usage settings on ChatGPT's desktop app or website. It restores eligible allowances before their scheduled renewal but doesn't permanently increase them.
Once you've used your complimentary reset, you'll be back to consuming your allowance at the corrected rate.

articles.title: Bitcoin Turns Green Into Thanksgiving as Crypto Demand Nerves Continue
articles.text:
Bitcoin price eyes $61K as Talos warns of thin Thanksgiving liquidity
Bitcoin joined US stock futures in a modest relief rally as Talos questioned crypto demand and the broader outlook for the AI trade.
Bitcoin (BTC) reclaimed $60,000 at Wednesday’s daily close as selling pressure eased across crypto markets.
Key points:
- Bitcoin closed above $60,000 as US stock-market futures trended higher into the Thanksgiving holiday.
- Talos warned that the rebound lacked sustained demand despite a rally following Jensen Huang’s return as Nvidia CEO.
- Bitcoin’s annualized downside volatility on Binance reached 46%, compared with 19% for upside volatility, according to CryptoQuant data.
Talos questions crypto demand as Thanksgiving arrives
Data from TradingView showed BTC/USD 0.8% higher at noon UTC on Thursday, approaching $61,000.
BTC/USD 1-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView

Macro asset weekly performance through Nov. 24. Source: Talos

“That’s roughly 2.4 times more volatility on the way down than on the way up,” a CryptoQuant community analyst noted.

BTC rolling 30-day upside vs. downside volatility. Source: CryptoQuant

articles.title: Elon Musk Says ‘Multiplanetary’ SpaceX Could Be Worth $118 Quintillion. Yes, Quintillion
articles.text:
In brief
- Elon Musk claims SpaceX could eventually be worth one million times the size of today's global economy.
- The billionaire pledged two SpaceX shares to every American child, urging recipients to hold onto their stock.
- Musk has a history of extravagant predictions involving Mars colonization, autonomous vehicles, and the valuations of his companies.
Forget becoming the world's first trillionaire, that’s spare change for Elon Musk.
The SpaceX CEO said Thursday that his company could eventually be worth a million times the current global economy, following an announcement that he and his company would give two SpaceX shares to every child in America.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short SPCX with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
“If SpaceX succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy, it will be worth about a million times the current global economy,” Musk tweeted. “These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them.”
For those unfamiliar with numbers that large, the World Bank puts global GDP at $118.35 trillion in 2025. Using that figure as a reference, Musk is talking about a company worth roughly $118 quintillion.
“I recommend holding on to your shares,” Elon wrote.
If SpaceX succeeds in making life multiplanetary and harnessing even a millionth of the Sun’s energy, it will be worth about a million times the current global economy.
These are obviously absurdly difficult goals, but there is a path to achieving them.
I recommend holding on…
— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 26, 2026
He didn’t disclose taking any substances before writing that tweet.
The figure Elon talks about is basically 118 followed by 18 zeros or approximately 68 million times SpaceX's current market capitalization. Comparing a company's valuation with annual economic output isn't an apples-to-apples comparison, but it illustrates the scale of Musk's ambitions.
The comments came hours after the Federal Communications Commission authorized SpaceX to deploy up to one million satellites designed to operate as solar-powered data centers in space.
It sounds cool and all, but capturing a millionth of the Sun's energy is a considerably more ambitious undertaking. The Sun generates approximately 380 septillion watts, meaning SpaceX would need to capture some 380 quintillion watts to meet Musk's goal.
As for the giveaway, SpaceX's official announcement specifies that its contribution will go to currently active Trump Accounts, tax-advantaged investment accounts for American children, with Musk personally matching the donation.
The combined pledge could be worth approximately $18 billion, per Reuters.
Elon Musk’s extraordinary predictions
Musk has a peculiar relationship with big numbers and deadlines, especially when discussing the future of his own companies.
In 2016, the billionaire predicted that SpaceX could launch humans toward Mars in 2024, with the astronauts arriving in 2025. Humanity is not even close to that goal even this decade.
Three years later, during Tesla's Autonomy Day, Musk told investors that the electric vehicle manufacturer would have more than one million autonomous robotaxis on the road by 2020. Tesla was still preparing to launch its commercial robotaxi operations five years after that deadline.
Tesla and SpaceX merger officially announced by...?
During an earnings call in October 2022, Musk also said he saw a path for Tesla's valuation to exceed those of Apple and Saudi Aramco combined, which together were worth more than $4 trillion at the time.
More recently, he argued that artificial intelligence will surpass humanity's combined intelligence within five years, urging AI firms to cooperate on safety.
Musk's social media pronouncements have occasionally proved expensive, too. His infamous 2018 tweet about having secured funding to take Tesla private at $420 per share resulted in a $40 million settlement with the Securities and Exchange Commission, split evenly between Musk and Tesla. A jury subsequently found them not liable in a separate investor lawsuit.
Unlike his previous predictions, Musk hasn't given shareholders a deadline for reaching his astronomical SpaceX valuation.
He did provide a more terrestrial deadline for his stock giveaway, though. SpaceX's contribution is scheduled for December, with Musk's personal contribution following in June 2027, when the restrictions preventing him from transferring his shares expire.
Until then, two SpaceX shares are worth about $255.

articles.title: Zcash Devs Urge Users to Migrate 2% of ZEC Supply to Accelerate Sapling Pool Retirement
articles.text:
Zcash devs urge users to migrate 2% of ZEC supply to accelerate Sapling pool retirement
Zcash developers urged users to move funds out of an older shielded transaction pool over concerns that AI advances could compromise its cryptography.
Zcash development team Zakura urged the community to accelerate the proposed retirement of Sapling, an older shielded transaction pool, which holds nearly 2% of the total Zcash token supply.
Zakura, led by co-founder Sean Bowe and developer Dev Ojha, told community members on Wednesday to start migrating their funds from Sapling, which holds about 400,000 Zcash (ZEC) tokens, worth about $302 million.
Zakura recommended a network upgrade to stop new deposits into Sapling, while keeping withdrawals open to allow existing holders to migrate their funds to Zcash’s newer shielded pool, Ironwood.
AI-accelerated mathematical advancements could eventually undermine Sapling’s pairing-based cryptography and put funds at risk by allowing attackers to forge transaction proofs and potentially create counterfeit ZEC, Zakura warned. Ironwood uses a different proof system that does not rely on similar pairings. Dev Ojha proposed making the Sapling pool withdrawal-only in April 2026.
On June 3, Zcash developers temporarily suspended Orchard transactions after discovering a vulnerability in the shielded pool. Functionality was restored later that day through an emergency upgrade. The Zcash Foundation said there was no evidence that the vulnerability was exploited.
Related: Anthropic’s Mythos AI finds no more ‘serious’ bugs in Zcash: Wilcox

articles.title: Cournot Raises $5M to Build AI-Native Oracle for Verifiable Intelligence
articles.text:
In brief
- Cournot, an AI-based oracle backed by YZi Labs, has raised $5 million in a strategic round co-led by Paper Ventures and Beam Foundation.
- The firm uses AI to decide whether real-world conditions have been met, with its system recording every source and reasoning step so outcomes can be audited.
- It says its oracle has settled more than $1.41 billion in notional value across 29,200 resolutions, with 99.8% finalized without dispute.
Cournot, a startup building an AI-native oracle that helps applications and AI agents understand and verify real-world events, has raised $5 million in a strategic funding round co-led by Paper Ventures and Beam Foundation, the company tweeted on Thursday.
The firm was previously backed by YZi Labs, the investment firm of Binance founder Changpeng "CZ" Zhao, through its EASY Residency Season 3 program. Cournot said it will use the funding to develop its products, expand integrations on BNB Chain and other ecosystems, and move into areas including real-world assets, trading, parametric insurance, private credit and AI agents.
Cournot has raised $5M co-led by @papervc and @BeamFDN following earlier backing from @yzilabs through @EASYResidency S3, to build the verifiable intelligence layer for onchain applications and AI agents.
Cournot's mission is to expand what oracles can do: from structured data… pic.twitter.com/u0GnIBYFOO
— Cournot Protocol (@CournotProtocol) November 26, 2026
"As more financial activity and autonomous systems move onchain, the infrastructure around them needs to evolve beyond simply delivering data," Danish Chaudhry, founder of co-lead investor Paper Ventures, said in a statement. Cournot is making real-world intelligence "more verifiable, auditable, and usable by both applications and AI agents," he added.
Oracles bring outside information onto blockchains, so smart contracts can act on it. Most deliver structured data, such as asset prices. Cournot is aimed at questions that need interpretation, such as whether a real-world event has happened or whether the available evidence meets a contract's rules.
Its Resolution Oracle uses AI to judge whether defined conditions have been met, while its Intelligence Oracle provides probabilities, claims and supporting sources before an outcome is known.
How Proof of Reasoning works
Both products rely on a framework Cournot calls Proof of Reasoning, which is designed to show how an AI model reached a conclusion, rather than just the conclusion itself.
In a case study published in February, Cournot outlined a four-stage process. First, the system fixes what a question's terms mean before any evidence is gathered, and commits that definition as a cryptographic hash, so it cannot be reinterpreted later. It then collects evidence only from sources named in advance, within set time windows.
— Cournot Protocol (@CournotProtocol) February 7, 2026
Where a source may change, such as a government webpage, Cournot uses zkTLS, a cryptographic technique that proves a website displayed certain information at a given time, to keep a tamper-proof record. Finally, the AI's reasoning can only draw on that verified evidence, and its verdict follows from the predefined rules, leaving a trail that can be audited and challenged.
The case study used a Polymarket market on whether there would be another U.S. government shutdown. Cournot has also cited a November 2025 shutdown market in which traders who correctly predicted the end date lost, because the Office of Personnel Management's website was updated a day after President Donald Trump signed the funding bill.
Beyond prediction markets
Cournot is also targeting the growing agent economy, in which autonomous AI agents need reliable outside information before making financial or operational decisions. Through its Intelligence Oracle skill, agents can request structured probabilities for events, the exact claims being assessed and supporting sources, and build those evidence-backed assessments into their own decision-making, according to the company.
As of November 25, 2026, Cournot’s Resolution Oracle had settled more than $1.41 billion in notional value across more than 29,200 resolutions, with 99.8% finalized without a dispute, the firm said. The company said resolutions had grown fivefold over the past three months and that the business is already profitable. Its oracles are used by prediction markets, agentic trading venues and trading card game platforms.
Its Intelligence Oracle Skill has scaled to more than 20,000 installs, 18,000 paying wallets and 967,000 paid calls, and the business is already profitable, according to Cournot. Its oracles are used by prediction markets, agentic trading venues and trading card game platforms.
Cournot argues the same problem applies well beyond betting, envisaging AI systems that could settle crop insurance by analyzing satellite imagery and local reports, or pay out on software contracts by reading a project's GitHub activity, with an auditable record of how each decision was reached.
"Human voting is slow and contestable, and black-box AI is fast but unaccountable," Cournot co-founder Daniel Wang said in a statement.
Cournot said that at no stage is an outcome decided by a token-weighted vote. That is how disputes are settled on prediction market Polymarket, which relies on UMA's Optimistic Oracle, a system that has drawn criticism after disputed outcomes. Polymarket has also integrated Chainlink data feeds for markets that hinge on asset prices.
Cournot pointed to a November 2025 post in which CZ said the industry needed more oracles, adding that "one or two is not enough."
In the longer term, the firm said its aim is to extend oracles beyond structured data into interpreting real-world events, providing verifiable intelligence and, eventually, taking action on behalf of AI agents within set policies. As more applications and autonomous agents operate onchain, the company expects demand to grow for infrastructure that helps them understand real-world information and weigh the evidence before they act.

articles.title: Switzerland’s First Spot Bitcoin ETF Rises 0.6% in First Hour
articles.text:
Switzerland’s first spot Bitcoin ETF ticks up 0.6% in opening hour
The spot Bitcoin ETF will be backed by Bitcoin held in cold storage at a Swiss bank, unlike prior Bitcoin ETPs structured as debt securities.
Switzerland’s first spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) had a quiet debut Thursday morning, with 1,601 shares changing hands on its Swiss franc listing by the first hour of trading.
BIT Asset Management’s Bitcoin Fund (BBIT) on SIX Swiss Exchange opened at 8 Swiss francs (about $9.6) per share and rose 0.6% to 8.05 francs at 9 am UTC.
BBIT holds Bitcoin (BTC) directly and trades in both Swiss francs and US dollars, giving investors exposure to Bitcoin through a regulated Swiss investment fund, SIX said Thursday.
The fund is issued by Pernet von Ballmoos (PvB), with BIT Asset Management acting as sponsor, asset manager and distributor, while its Bitcoin holdings are custodied offline at a Swiss bank. The ETF is subject to Switzerland’s Collective Investment Schemes Act, which governs investment funds and provides investor protection measures.
Switzerland already has Bitcoin exchange-traded products that are structured as debt securities, but BBIT is the first fund that directly holds spot Bitcoin. FINMA approved the launch of the Bitcoin ETF in October.

articles.title: Galaxy Research Withdraws Call That Bitcoin's Bear Market Is Over
articles.text:
In brief
- Galaxy Research has withdrawn its October call that Bitcoin's bear market ended in June, after the technical signal behind it failed.
- Galaxy said a daily close below Bitcoin's June 30 low of $58,525 would mark the start of a move to a materially lower low.
- Every prior break of a standing bear market low led at least 17% lower, Galaxy found, implying a floor near $48,500 or a median target near $28,200.
Galaxy Research has withdrawn its call that Bitcoin's bear market ended in June, saying the signal that underpinned it has failed.
"We withdraw our call that the bear market ended in June," the firm wrote in a report sent to clients on Tuesday. It said a daily close below Bitcoin's June 30 closing low of $58,525 would mark "the start of a move to a materially lower low."
Did you know?

Bitcoin is currently changing hands at around $60,600, up 3.4% over the past 24 hours, according to Decrypt data. It fell as low as $57,308 during that period, as inflation data and proposed U.S. tariffs weighed on markets.
What broke
In an October 26 report, Galaxy's head of research, Alex Thorn, argued that Bitcoin had bottomed in June, in part because it had climbed back above its 50-week moving average in September after 44 weeks below it. In past cycles, such a sustained recovery above that average had only come after a bear market's low.
That reclaim lasted seven weeks. Bitcoin closed below the 50-week average in the week ended November 8, and the following week fell below its 200-week average, which Galaxy describes as historically the floor. On an intraday basis, Bitcoin has already set a new bear market low, falling to $55,100 on November 21, below its July 1 intraday low. On closing prices, the June 30 low of $58,525 is still intact.
Previous bear markets
In seven previous bear markets in which Bitcoin closed below a low that had held for at least 60 days, the eventual bottom came at least 17% lower, with a median of 52%, according to Galaxy. Applied to the June low, that would put Bitcoin at about $48,500 at the shallowest and $28,200 at the median.
The firm said the evidence points two ways. By the calendar, this bear market is already older than any before it, 412 days after Bitcoin's October 2025 record. By depth, it looks unfinished: Bitcoin's 53% decline compares with 77% to 93% in previous bear markets, and it has not yet closed below its realized price of $53,205, the average price at which all coins last moved, something every prior bear did for at least 140 days. Only two of the 13 bottom signals Galaxy tracks have been met.
BTC price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
Galaxy said a weekly close back above the 200-week average, now $68,159, and then the 50-week average, now $74,401, would move it back toward its October view.
Tim Sun, senior researcher at HashKey, told Decrypt he agreed the market remained in a bear phase, but said a longer bear market need not mean a deeper one. As Bitcoin is pulled into global asset allocation, its price is driven increasingly by "macro liquidity, interest-rate expectations, and institutional risk appetite, rather than solely following the crypto market's traditional four-year cycle," he said.
ETF outflows continue
U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $453.1 million in net outflows on Wednesday, their seventh straight day of withdrawals, according to SoSoValue data. That brings November's net outflows to $5.39 billion, extending the funds' worst month on record.
Options traders are also positioning for further declines. Bitcoin's put/call open interest ratio on Deribit rose to 0.82 last week, its highest in more than a year, according to a weekly report from digital asset trading platform Talos.
"BTC's muted rebound shows the relief in equities has not translated into demand for crypto," Tanay Ved, senior research associate at Talos, said in the report. "Until short covering turns into net buy pressure and sustained spot demand, the move remains fragile heading into thin holiday liquidity."

articles.title: UK Regulator Plans Tighter DeFi Rules After $6.3B Binance Hack
articles.text:
UK regulator plans tighter DeFi rules, citing $6.3B Binance hack: Report
North Korea-linked hackers used DeFi protocols to launder stolen Binance funds, while US prosecutors moved to recover more than $1.1 billion in crypto.
The United Kingdom’s financial regulator is reportedly planning to push ahead with tighter restrictions on decentralized finance (DeFi), citing money laundering risks highlighted by the $6.3 billion Binance hack.
On Thursday, the Financial Times reported that the Financial Conduct Authority (FCA) plans to proceed with proposed authorization requirements for DeFi platforms, citing concerns over fraud, money laundering and insufficient consumer protections.
Jane Moore, the FCA’s head of payments and digital assets, said the speed and scale at which stolen funds move through DeFi platforms could undermine efforts to freeze assets and prevent money laundering.
Following the Oct. 29 Binance hack, attackers linked to North Korea used decentralized protocols, including THORChain, to move stolen assets. On Monday, US prosecutors moved to recover more than $1.1 billion in cryptocurrency stolen during the attack.
The FCA also reportedly plans to require all UK retail equity orders, including those involving tokenized stocks, to be executed on regulated platforms.
On Oct. 21, the FCA launched consultations on DeFi guidance and the scope of its broader crypto regulatory framework. Both consultations closed on Nov. 18, with final guidance expected in January 2027, ahead of the new regime’s implementation on Oct. 25, 2027.
Cointelegraph reached out to the FCA for comment but had not received an immediate response.
Related: Binance says it obtained $6.5B worldwide freezing order after hack

articles.title: UK Regulator Cites Binance Hack as It Plans Tougher DeFi Rules Than US and EU: Report
articles.text:
In brief
- The FCA plans to require DeFi platforms to be authorized under its new crypto regime, pointing to the Binance hack as a reason for a stricter approach.
- Regulated UK crypto exchanges will not be allowed to execute retail trades on DeFi platforms, a divide the regulator said is deliberate.
- Industry figures from Aave Labs and Coinbase warned the UK risks falling behind the US and EU, which are building routes for regulated DeFi access.
Britain's Financial Conduct Authority plans to require decentralized finance platforms to be authorized under its incoming crypto rules, taking a harder line than regulators in the U.S. or EU, the Financial Times reported on Thursday.
FCA officials told the newspaper they were deliberately strict on DeFi because they saw a high risk of fraud, scams and money laundering, and because users had little ability to recover stolen funds or seek compensation.
The regulator pointed to the record $6.4 billion hack of Binance in October. While Binance is a centralized exchange, the hackers moved large sums through decentralized exchanges, which do not freeze stolen funds, swapping them into other tokens to make them harder to trace.
"The speed and scale at which stolen funds move through DeFi platforms can frustrate attempts to freeze and block" transfers, Jane Moore, the FCA's head of department for payments and digital assets, told the FT.
Did you know?
You can now act on the news you read: Go long or short ETH with perpetual futures, all from your Decrypt Money Account.
A 'clear divide'
The FCA's position means UK-regulated crypto trading platforms will not be allowed to execute retail trades on DeFi platforms. Moore said that divide between the regulated and unregulated sectors was deliberate, given the lack of consumer protections in DeFi.
The regulator also plans to require all UK retail orders for equities, tokenized or not, to be executed on a regulated platform, cutting off access to offshore DeFi venues for tokenized stocks. The same risk should be treated the same way, Jamie Bell, the FCA's head of capital markets, told the newspaper. The FCA and the Bank of England have set out a shared vision for tokenization within the regulated system.
After consulting on its wider crypto rules earlier this year, the FCA in October published draft guidance on how its rules apply to firms providing services that use or interact with DeFi. The consultation closed on November 18, and the regulator expects to publish final guidance in January 2027, ahead of its crypto regime taking effect on October 25, 2027.
ETH price on November 29, 4:59PM UTC
Industry pushback
Crypto firms argue the approach will leave UK investors without access to products such as tokenized equities and decentralized lending.
Linda Jeng, chief legal and policy officer at Aave Labs, which builds products for decentralized lending protocol Aave, called the FCA's position "highly problematic" and has written to the regulator asking it to clarify which DeFi service providers its rules would cover, according to the FT.
Coinbase's head of policy in Europe, Katie Harries, said that where the U.S. and EU are building rules for regulated DeFi access, the UK is "creating a prohibition." In September, the EU's European Securities and Markets Authority proposed a new regulated service under the bloc's MiCA rules for crypto firms that give customers access to DeFi protocols.
UK trade group CryptoUK has also urged the FCA not to treat DeFi developers as regulated by default, warning in its consultation response that parts of the proposed guidance go further than the law.
Orest Gavryliak, chief legal officer at DeFi aggregator 1inch, argued that financial crime is a challenge across all of finance, and that DeFi's transparency is a strength. "Every transaction is recorded on a public ledger, so illicit flows can be traced in a way that closed systems do not allow," he said.
A one-size-fits-all approach "would limit access to innovation without meaningfully reducing risk," Gavryliak said, adding that regulators could draw on industry tools such as wallet screening to design proportionate, risk-based rules.
Harry Halpin, CEO of decentralized VPN provider Nym, told Decrypt that a truly decentralized DeFi platform would be very hard to regulate, since there should be no central party to oversee. "If the government attempts then to block or censor access to these platforms, and so slowly built a Great Firewall of Britain, people will simply use a VPN," he said.

articles.title: Sky Seeks Emergency Vote on $25M Transfer Amid stUSDS Liquidity Crunch
articles.text:
Sky proposes emergency vote on $25M transfer amid liquidity stress
Sky’s Core Facilitator invoked the protocol’s emergency response process to expedite a vote rather than wait until the next scheduled vote on Dec. 3.
Decentralized finance (DeFi) protocol Sky has proposed an emergency governance vote to expedite the transfer to 25 million USDS to the Sky Frontier Foundation to pay down debt amid a liquidity crunch that has left stUSDS depositors struggling to withdraw their funds for more than two weeks.
On Wednesday, Sky’s Core Facilitator said it was invoking the protocol’s emergency response process to accelerate debt repayments in a bid to ease liquidity pressure, rather than wait until the next scheduled vote on Dec. 3. Repaying loans funded by the stUSDS lending pool would free up capital for depositors to withdraw.
The liquidity crisis developed as depositors pulled funds from the stUSDS lending pool, which provides USDS loans to borrowers using staked SKY tokens as collateral. Bitquery found that daily withdrawals reached about $14.2 million on Nov. 10, exhausting available liquidity.
At the time of writing, Spark data showed that nearly all of the pool’s $158.48 million in assets had been lent out, leaving just $3,270 available for withdrawals.
On Monday, Sky co-founder Rune Christensen acknowledged that his borrowing had contributed to the withdrawal crunch, saying he still owed about 77 million USDS.
The proposal follows a Sky lender’s call to use up to $50 million in protocol reserves to purchase SKY tokens from borrowers, enabling them to repay loans and free up withdrawal liquidity.
Related: Sky Protocol sees $2 billion in stablecoin withdrawals, disputes illicit fund claims

articles.title: Bought Nvidia stock during the 2017 crypto boom? You could qualify for a $290 million settlement
articles.text:
Quick Take
- A proposed $290 million cash deal would resolve shareholder claims over Nvidia’s disclosures about demand from crypto miners.
- Qualifying Nvidia common-stock investors would need to document their losses and submit a claim to share the net fund.
- The preliminary hearing is set for February 2027, and payouts depend on final approval and a separate distribution order.
Investors who bought or otherwise acquired Nvidia common stock from Aug. 10, 2017, through Nov. 15, 2018, could share in a proposed $290 million cash settlement if the court approves the deal and their claims qualify.
The parties filed the agreement on Nov. 24, and plaintiffs filed an unopposed motion for preliminary approval that day in federal court in Oakland.
The plaintiffs alleged that Nvidia and Jensen Huang misled investors about how much crypto miners contributed to sales of graphics chips Nvidia marketed for gaming.
They say shareholders suffered losses after the extent of Nvidia’s mining exposure emerged in 2018. Nvidia and Huang deny wrongdoing, and the settlement agreement contains no admission of liability.
The court certified the class in March, covering individuals and entities. Exclusions include the defendants, Nvidia officers and directors at relevant times, certain relatives and related entities, and the defendants’ liability insurers. Investors whose requests to opt out are accepted by the court are also excluded.
Class members seeking payment would have to file a paper or electronic claim by a court-set deadline, with documents supporting their claimed loss.
Under the proposed allocation, approved claimants would share the net fund in proportion to the losses the plan recognizes for their stock transactions.
The plan would use the investor’s documented transactions, including what they paid for the shares and what they received if they sold them, but the court would have to approve the allocation plan.
The net fund would include the cash settlement and accrued interest, less taxes, notice and administration costs, court-awarded legal fees and litigation expenses, and other court-approved costs.
Individual payments would depend on the amount left in the fund and the total recognized losses from approved claims.
The parties accepted a mediator’s recommendation on Sept. 24 and notified the court of their agreement on Oct. 22.
What has to happen before Nvidia payouts?
The public docket lists Feb. 4, 2027, at 2 p.m. for the preliminary-approval hearing before Judge Haywood S. Gilliam Jr. in Oakland.
If he grants preliminary approval, the proposed schedule calls for postcard notices to start going out and the claim form to be posted within 20 calendar days of the order. Claims would be due 90 calendar days after the notice date.
The plaintiffs propose a final hearing 130 calendar days after the preliminary order or as soon afterward as the court can accommodate. Payments would require final approval, the settlement taking effect, and a separate court order directing distribution to approved claimants.

articles.title: New York Wins $1.37B Judgment Against NovaTech Founders Who Fled the US
articles.text:
In brief
- A New York court ordered NovaTech founders Cynthia and Eddy Petion to pay $1.37 billion over a crypto Ponzi scheme that targeted Haitian communities.
- The scheme drew in hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide, including 11,000 New Yorkers, often through prayer groups and WhatsApp chats.
- The Petions fled the U.S. before a default judgment last year, raising questions over how much of the money victims will recover.
A New York court has ordered the founders of collapsed crypto trading platform NovaTech to pay $1.37 billion for running a Ponzi scheme that targeted Haitian immigrant communities, Attorney General Letitia James said on Wednesday.
Cynthia and Eddy Petion, along with NovaTech and related companies, are jointly liable for $1.13 billion in disgorgement plus $232.5 million in interest, for a total of $1,367,023,585, according to court documents in the case, which is before Justice Anar Rathod Patel in the Commercial Division of New York's Supreme Court.
We won a historic $1.3 billion judgment against the founders of crypto company NovaTech for defrauding hundreds of thousands of people, including Haitian immigrants in New York.
We'll always fight to bring fraudsters who take advantage of New Yorkers to justice.
— NY AG James (@NewYorkStateAG) November 25, 2026
Cynthia Petion and AWS Mining, a crypto mining company the couple promoted before founding NovaTech, were also ordered to pay a further $6.2 million combined for the AWS Mining scheme.
"NovaTech cruelly targeted immigrant families through faith and community groups with the promise of a better life while robbing them of their life savings," James said in a statement.
Did you know?

A default judgment
The judgment follows a default ruling in August 2025, after the Petions fled the country and failed to respond to the lawsuit. That ruling also banned them from the securities, commodities and crypto industries, and the court then decided how much they owed.
In October, James' office asked the court to set the damages at about $1.37 billion. The Petions failed to comply with a court order to provide a full accounting of payments to and from investors, according to the court documents.
Collecting the money may prove difficult. The couple was allegedly living in Panama when James first sued in June 2024, Reuters reported at the time.
Prayer groups and WhatsApp
James' office sued NovaTech and AWS Mining in June 2024, alleging that they targeted immigrant communities, particularly Haitian New Yorkers, through prayer groups, social media and WhatsApp chats, with false promises of high returns, while running illegal pyramid schemes. The schemes defrauded hundreds of thousands of investors worldwide, including about 11,000 New Yorkers, according to the attorney general.

Four promoters in the New York case, Martin Zizi, Frantz Ciceron, Ricardo Roy Sr. and James Corbett, have agreed to pay nearly $6 million and have been permanently banned from the securities, commodities and crypto industries.
