articles.title: Morpho’s largest euro stablecoin vault is €13.8 million short of covering its biggest depositor’s exit
articles.text:
Quick Take
- The EBA’s November report says more than half of circulating EURCV was supplied to a Morpho vault in July.
- Morpho’s app showed 107.2 million EURCV in available liquidity against a 120.99 million EURCV position on Nov. 26.
- Eligible EEA residents can request direct redemption, with cash due by the last business day of the month after checks clear.
Morpho’s largest listed vault for EUR CoinVertible (EURCV), a euro stablecoin, showed about 13.8 million EURCV less liquidity than its biggest address would need for a full exit on Nov. 26.
A withdrawal would return EURCV to a wallet, but eligible holders seeking euros directly from issuer SG-FORGE would follow a separate redemption timetable.
Morpho’s Steakhouse Prime EURCV vault on Ethereum showed 144.3 million EURCV in deposits and 107.2 million in displayed liquidity, including tokens the app could pull from other lending markets.
The top address accounted for 121 million EURCV (83.8%), according to the same page. Steakhouse Prime was the largest EURCV vault by assets in Morpho’s public ranking.
The comparison assumes the top address sought to withdraw its entire position at that moment. Morpho’s public data show balances by address, which can pool funds for more than one owner.
The European Banking Authority’s Nov. 25 report on stablecoins in decentralized finance found that, in its July analysis, more than half of circulating EURCV was supplied to a Morpho vault.
A standard vault withdrawal draws on idle tokens and funds that can be pulled from the market designated for withdrawals. At Ethereum block 26,500,641, Morpho’s address-level position data put that route’s limit at 103.1 million EURCV against a position worth 120.99 million.
That left about 17.9 million EURCV beyond the ordinary withdrawal limit at the indexed block.
Under Morpho’s withdrawal rules, the app can pull available funds from other markets when the vault configuration allows it, a process called forced deallocation.
Morpho’s withdrawal-options data showed about 102.8 million EURCV idle and about $340,000 available in the designated market, plus about 4 million that could be pulled from other markets, based on rounded amounts.
That last source of funds explains why the app showed more liquidity than a standard withdrawal could use. What a depositor can withdraw depends on what is still available when the transaction executes.
In a lending market where borrowers are using most of the funds, repayments or fresh deposits can free up tokens for another withdrawal.
On eligible vaults, Morpho also offers an in-kind exit that can return some EURCV to the wallet and convert part of the redeemed amount into a direct position in a lending market.
When withdrawn tokens become bank euros
SG-FORGE’s September 2026 EURCV white paper says holders resident in the European Economic Area can request direct redemption at one euro per token.
The issuer applies identity, anti-money-laundering, sanctions and other checks, and may require the holder to transfer the tokens to it.
SG-FORGE says it will transfer euros to the holder’s cash account by the last business day of the month after the checks clear. For example, if the checks clear in December, the white paper’s timetable sets the payment deadline for the last business day of January.

articles.title: 1Password Confirms Data Breach, Says Vaults Unaffected
articles.text:
1Password hacker stole customer names and emails, but vaults safe
The password manager, which is used by millions of people to store their login credentials, said customer vaults were unaffected by the breach.
Password manager 1Password disclosed Wednesday that an attacker stole names and email addresses belonging to some customers after breaking into its backend systems.
Customer vaults and their contents were not affected, but 1Password said the breach could lead to phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls.
The company said it began investigating last Thursday after discovering signs an attacker had gained access to an employee’s GitHub account. The attacker used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, allowing them to extract customer data.
“This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker,” the company said.
The password manager lets people store passwords for different websites and apps in one encrypted vault. 1Password says millions of people and more than 200,000 businesses use its service.
The company also partnered with crypto wallet provider Phantom in 2022 to let users save their wallet passwords and recovery phrases in 1Password.
Following the attack, 1Password said it has since disabled the affected GitHub account, removed the attackers’ access, rotated all internal credentials potentially exposed, among other measures. It also said it has not found any evidence of user account takeovers or compromises from the attack.
Related: Chainalysis says breach exposed password hashes and live tokens

articles.title: XRP sellers could lose an extra $3,146 on a large trade if five accounts pull their buy orders
articles.text:
Quick Take
- A ledger reconstruction put five accounts at 72% of XRP/RLUSD trading volume in the 24 hours ending Nov. 25.
- The same five addresses supplied most trading volume in fills of at least 1,000 XRP across three matched sessions.
- Removing their buy orders cut funded RLUSD by 86% in the model and sent most of the 100,000 XRP sale to the pool.
Five XRP Ledger accounts supplied 72% of one day’s trading volume in XRP against Ripple USD (RLUSD), according to XRPL.to.
For a test of the next day’s order book, CryptoSlate selected the five addresses that led the Nov. 25 session in fills of at least 1,000 XRP, then simulated removing their buy orders.
Funded RLUSD in the first 100 buy offers fell from about 63,925 to 8,805. In the model, the matching pool, a standing reserve of both assets, took most of a 100,000 XRP sale after the removal. A seller would receive about 3.3% less RLUSD than with the full sample.
The last XRP/USD trade on Kraken was $0.94935 when the ticker was checked at 13:07:24 UTC on Nov. 26. On the ledger exchange itself, XRP/RLUSD accounted for 84% of all volume measured in XRP over the seven days covered by XRPL.to’s reconstruction.
In the 24 hours ending at 01:30 UTC on Nov. 25, XRPL.to’s reconstruction counted 25,801 fills moving about 6.3 million XRP. Traders took resting offers from 142 accounts or traded against the automated pool.
The biggest account, whose ledger address starts with rpiFwLYi, supplied 41% of executed volume. Together, the five largest supplied 72%, and the pool accounted for 3%.
A replay through the public trade history endpoint yielded 6.32 million XRP and counted 25,712 fills for the same window, 89 fewer than the published tally.
The index can group multiple executions into one transaction row. In one row covering 525.58 XRP, the validated transaction showed about 514 tokens went to one account’s buy orders and about 12 tokens to another’s.
To test whether concentration persisted, CryptoSlate used XRPL.to records and split combined fills using validated ledger changes.
The comparison covered same-pair fills of at least 1,000 XRP in three 24-hour windows ending at 01:30 UTC on Nov. 24, 25 and 26. The same five addresses, selected by Nov. 25 qualifying volume, accounted for about 71%, 88%, and 79% of qualifying volume, respectively.
The address starting with rpiFwLYi led the middle session, with about half the qualifying volume. An address starting with rURtT5MM led the sessions on either side.
That left the same group with a large share in all three windows even as the leading address changed, and the turnover includes trades in which the addresses gave or received XRP.
What an XRP seller could get at one ledger
The two sides of the XRP Ledger’s order book draw on different inventories. A resting order to buy XRP is funded in RLUSD, which the seller receives. A resting order to sell XRP draws on the seller’s inventory.
The relevant depth for a seller is the RLUSD that buyers can deliver at the displayed prices.
At validated ledger 108584374, which closed at 13:09:20 UTC on Nov. 26, the first 100 buy offers could take about 67,549 XRP at the displayed prices.
Excluding buy offers from the five large-fill leaders left room for about 9,302 XRP in that same sample. The funded RLUSD in the sample fell about 86%.
The matching XRP/RLUSD pool held about 1.99 million XRP and 1.89 million RLUSD. The model applied its standard 0.315% fee and allocated each portion of the sale to the better available price.
The test held the remaining offers fixed and used only the sampled book and the direct pool, with deeper orders, replacement orders, and additional fees outside the simulation.
In the model, a 1,000 sale returned 947.96 RLUSD with the full order sample and 947.87 without the five addresses’ buy orders. At 10,000, proceeds slipped from 9,474.85 to 9,470.90 RLUSD. At 100,000, proceeds fell from 94,197.18 to 91,050.74 RLUSD.
The pool took about 32,451 XRP in the first case and 90,698 after the orders were removed.
The pool’s price worsens as sellers draw down its RLUSD reserves, which is why a large trade can clear and still return less.

articles.title: Senators Urge SEC to Scrap Crypto, Tokenized Stock Exemptions
articles.text:
Senate Democrats urge SEC to scrap crypto, tokenized stock exemptions
US Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Van Hollen, among others, have taken aim at two recent SEC efforts to ease regulatory requirements for the crypto industry.
US Senators Elizabeth Warren and Chris Van Hollen have urged the US Securities and Exchange Commission to drop a proposal that would allow eligible crypto projects to raise funds from US investors without registering their offerings and revoke an exemption for tokenized stock platforms.
In two letters sent to SEC Chair Paul Atkins on Tuesday, the Democratic lawmakers argued that the agency had exceeded its statutory authority in both cases and that the moves will put investors at risk.
“Together, the letters raise concerns about the SEC’s efforts to carve out special treatment for crypto assets and tokenized securities at the expense of investor protections and market integrity,” they said.
Both SEC measures drew crypto industry support, as they came at a time when the CLARITY Act struggled to advance in Congress. The Regulation Crypto Assets was first introduced in August when the landmark crypto legislation was stalled, while the tokenized stock exemption came out in September, two days after the CLARITY Act fell short of the 60 votes needed to advance.
Senators warn of a “shadow stock market”
The letters also come just a day after OKXICE, a joint venture between crypto exchange OKX and New York Stock Exchange parent Intercontinental Exchange, launched a round-the-clock trading venue for tokenized US securities under the exemption on Monday.
The tokenized stock exemption allows qualifying platforms to offer blockchain-based trading of tokenized US stocks without registering as exchanges.
SEC lists four other entities that intend to use the exemption, including TSV LLC (which commenced operation in early November), Kephas Corporation d/b/a Perpetuals.com, Formation Securities LLC and Fairmint TSV LLC.
Van Hollen, Warren and two other senators urged the SEC to withdraw the order, warning the order could create a “shadow stock market” that falls outside of regulatory protections.
“We are particularly troubled by the order’s sweeping exemption of TSVs from fundamental registration requirements,” they said.
They also argued the order places an “unreasonable burden” on publicly traded companies by allowing third parties to tokenize their securities unless the issuer objects within 30 days.
“This effectively establishes an opt-out regime in which companies must continuously monitor tokenization activity and respond to potentially numerous requests from different platforms to prevent unauthorized trading of tokenized versions of their shares.”
Related: Trump’s SEC nominee Johnson backs formal rulemaking for tokenized stock trading
The senators also argued venues are exempt from rules requiring them to display their best prices to traders. “These protections are foundational to the fairness and efficiency of our equity markets,” they said.
Atkins previously described the five-year exemption as an interim measure to allow onchain trading of certain US stocks while the agency considers longer-term rules.
Senators target SEC’s proposed fundraising exemption
In a separate letter, Warren, Van Hollen and Senator Tina Smith urged the SEC to withdraw its Regulation Crypto Assets Proposal, arguing that the proposal only serves to help crypto assets “escape” from the SEC’s regulatory regime.
The proposal would allow eligible crypto projects to raise up to $5 million over four years under a startup exemption or up to $75 million in a 12-month period under a separate fundraising exemption, without registering the offerings with the SEC.
The senators argued these exemptions would let crypto issuers raise money without prior SEC review, particularly the $5 million startup exemption, which would allow early-stage projects to raise money without providing financial statements.
“The proposal rationalizes the startup exemption with the idea that these offerings are from startups, and its only limitation is a $5 million offering cap. However, the exemption does nothing to actually protect investors – it simply means that the SEC is willing for investors to be defrauded in $5 million increments,” they said.
The SEC has previously said that the exemptions would require issuers to give investors written disclosures, and federal anti-fraud and anti-manipulation rules would still apply.
Cointelegraph reached out to the SEC for comment.
Magazine: Can the SEC and CFTC’s pro-crypto rules be overturned? Legal opinion

articles.title: LayerZero locks early ZRO deposits behind validators users cannot choose
articles.text:
Quick Take
- LayerZero named Kakao Pay and ZAN as planned Zero validators and said Four Pillars will operate for Samsung Card.
- Zero’s portal splits early deposits equally across initial validators, while the full distribution of launch voting weight remains undisclosed.
- LayerZero expects unstaking to open by March 31, 2027, with a cooldown of up to seven days after that.
LayerZero named Kakao Pay and ZAN among the first validators for its Zero blockchain on Nov. 25 and said Four Pillars would run validator operations on behalf of Samsung Card.
The operators are slated to help confirm blocks when Zero opens to the public, a launch planned for Nov. 30.
The appointments show who will exercise some of the voting weight tied to early deposits of ZRO, the token that backs validator votes on Zero.
Under LayerZero’s staking terms, the portal automatically spreads early stake equally across the initial validators. Holders have no say in which validators receive it and no way to withdraw early.
LayerZero says its launch validators will span Asia, Europe and North America. Its Nov. 25 announcement names the Asia-Pacific participants and identifies Four Pillars as the operator for Samsung Card.
Validators check proofs that transactions were processed correctly and vote on blocks. A validator’s vote carries more weight when more ZRO is staked behind it, according to LayerZero’s staking guide.
The project’s February technical paper describes a design in which operators can validate without putting up their own tokens, and the network selects its consensus committee in proportion to stake.
LayerZero’s staking terms define genesis as the private mainnet launch, which the terms expected on Nov. 23, and that was also the date LayerZero gave for the opening of early staking. For public mainnet, the company says staked ZRO will be visible in Zero Explorer once the network goes live.
On Nov. 24, LayerZero said the LayerZero Foundation had completed 100 million ZRO in pre-genesis staking in two transactions of 50 million ZRO each.
The portal’s rewards calculator shows 300 million ZRO in an illustrative scenario that assumes 30% participation.
When early stakers can withdraw
A holder who disagrees with a validator during the lock has no option in the portal to redirect the stake or exit the position, and the lock covers the staked tokens and any rewards.
LayerZero expects unstaking to open by March 31, 2027, and says that date may change. Once unstaking opens, it can take up to seven days, so moving ZRO off Zero to another chain may require a later upgrade.
LayerZero describes a 1% annual issuance target as the basis for the reward pool, and the terms set an initial validator commission of 10% on rewards. A holder’s share depends on how much ZRO they stake, how long they stake it, and how much others commit.
Any rewards compound into the locked position, and the staking guide says validators will set their own commission after the initial period.
Until unstaking opens, stakers can track their balances, but the selected validator set exercises the consensus votes backed by those deposits. The public launch is the next chance to see which of the announced validators come online.

articles.title: AI Labs Likely Sitting on Cryptography ‘Bombshells’
articles.text:
AI labs likely sitting on cryptography ‘bombshells,’ computer scientist says
AI is driving a massive wave of mathematical breakthroughs which could have implications for cryptography.
(Update Nov. 26 at 11:39pm UTC): This article has been updated to include comments from Quantus founder Christopher Smith.
Theoretical computer scientist Scott Aaronson says leading AI laboratories are likely sitting on undisclosed breakthroughs in cryptography.
In a blog post on Wednesday, Aaronson, a former OpenAI researcher and professor at The University of Texas at Austin, warned that algorithms emerging from AI-driven mathematical advances will eventually break currently deployed cryptosystems.
“I’m virtually certain, from multiple reliable sources, that the AI labs are now sitting on one or more bombshells in that area,” Aaronson said. “However, until I either see details or hear directly from someone at a lab, I feel much, much less confident about the specific nature of those bombshells.”
The remarks add to concerns that AI’s accelerating mathematical capabilities could eventually undermine the cryptography used to secure crypto wallets and blockchain transactions. Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin and researcher Justin Drake raised those concerns in October.
AI tackles longstanding mathematical problems
Recent weeks have illustrated the pace at which AI has been able to overcome previously unsolvable math problems.
On Friday, Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge released an AI-assisted proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis, one of the most famous unsolved problems in mathematics.
Alpöge developed it with an unreleased version of Claude over roughly six weeks, spanning 17 million lines of Lean code. The proof was later verified as correct by Lean FRO and the Mathlib Initiative.
Days later, both Anthropic and OpenAI released proofs of the VP versus VNP conjecture, described as an algebraic cousin of P versus NP, another major unsolved problem in theoretical computer science.
In October, OpenAI released 722 AI-generated math manuscripts covering 372 problem areas on GitHub, which has since been nicknamed the “mathocalypse.”
“This past week — is very much like I would’ve always imagined the beginning of an AI singularity to look and feel like,” said Aaronson.
Related: AI poses greater threat to Bitcoin than quantum computing, Swan founder says
One of the rumors, according to Aaronson, is that one or both of the AI labs have solved “Factoring in P,” referring to a polynomial-time factoring algorithm — a breakthrough that could threaten RSA cryptography.
However, Christopher Smith, founder and CEO of Quantus, told Cointelegraph that while frontier labs have shown impressive results, there is no proof that factoring or discrete logarithm problems could be solved efficiently.
“These questions are naturally of great interest to anyone who works with technology, particularly in the blockchain industry, since a reduction of security for the elliptic curves could be catastrophic,” Smith said.
Aaronson declined to offer any insight on the idea that ECDSA, a digital signature scheme used by Bitcoin, had been broken.
“Crucially, don’t want the cryptography part of the story to overshadow the intellectual enormity of what’s happening,” said Aaronson.
“If, in these days of long-prophesied revelation and wonders and terrors, your main worry is your Bitcoin wallet, then go somewhere else for rumors about whether or not ECDSA is broken or whatever. I don’t have what you’re looking for here.”
Magazine: ‘Bunker mode’ won’t protect your crypto, critics say

articles.title: Chainlink jumps 10% as its Wall Street ambitions gain momentum on two fronts
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Chainlink rose 10% to $9.20 as Fidelity filed for a spot LINK ETF after enabling direct token purchases on its crypto platform.
- Fidelity's 57 million investors and Chainlink's 24/7 pricing infrastructure create new avenues for investment and commercial adoption.
- Existing Chainlink ETFs face their first monthly net outflows, testing whether Fidelity can revive investor demand.
Chainlink's LINK token climbed 10% over the past 24 hours to $9.20 as the network deepened its integration with traditional finance.
The rally comes as Fidelity Investments filed to launch a spot Chainlink exchange-traded fund (ETF), a day after enabling direct LINK trading on its cryptocurrency platform.
Meanwhile, Chainlink has expanded its financial market data infrastructure to support round-the-clock trading and lending involving tokenized stocks, commodities and other real-world assets, including during market holidays such as Thanksgiving.
Fidelity targets $176 million Chainlink ETF market
On Nov. 25, Fidelity submitted a registration statement to the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) for its proposed Fidelity Chainlink Fund, which would trade on Nasdaq under the ticker FLNK.
The fund would hold LINK directly, with Anchorage Digital, BitGo and Coinbase Custody safeguarding its assets. It would support cash and in-kind share creations and redemptions but would not stake its underlying tokens.
The filing came a day after Fidelity added LINK, AAVE and UNI to its Fidelity Crypto platform, expanding its customers' access to digital assets.
While eligible Fidelity Crypto customers can now purchase LINK directly, the proposed ETF would extend that access to investors seeking exposure through conventional brokerage accounts.
The consecutive moves could substantially broaden LINK's investor base. Fidelity serves approximately 57 million individual investors and reported $7.9 trillion in managed assets and $20.1 trillion in assets under administration at the end of September, making it one of the largest financial services firms in the US.
However, Fidelity is entering a market where investor appetite has weakened considerably.
According to SoSoValue data, Grayscale and Bitwise's spot Chainlink ETFs have attracted $176 million in cumulative net inflows since their respective launches. However, the funds recorded net inflows for just one day in November, putting them on course for their first month of net withdrawals since the market's inception.
Daily net flows for GLNK and CLNK through Nov. 25. Values follow Maketo's displayed rounding and totals are approximate, and non-trading days are excluded.
The slowdown in demand, coupled with LINK's price decline, has reduced the funds' combined net assets by approximately 33%, from $238.2 million at the end of September to $158.6 million on Nov. 25.
Fidelity's extensive retail and financial advisory network could help revive demand, but limited fresh capital could also intensify competition among issuers.
With Fidelity yet to disclose its management fee or launch date, the terms of its offering could determine how effectively it competes with Grayscale and Bitwise for LINK investors.
Chainlink brings traditional assets into 24/7 markets
Beyond expanding investment access to LINK, Chainlink is positioning its infrastructure to capture growing demand for financial markets that operate outside traditional exchange hours.
On Nov. 26, the decentralized oracle network introduced Chainlink 24/7 on its X account, a market data service that extends pricing coverage for traditional financial assets to weekends and public holidays.
The service builds on Chainlink's existing 24/5 infrastructure, which provides pricing for more than $1.6 billion in tokenized equities across six blockchains and supports platforms including Ondo, xStocks, Robinhood, and Coinbase.
Previously, blockchain-based financial applications struggled to value traditional assets when their underlying markets closed, limiting trading opportunities and complicating collateral management.
Chainlink's new service addresses that gap by combining traditional market data during active trading sessions with perpetual-futures-derived pricing when exchanges are closed.
The infrastructure could support continuous trading in tokenized assets, derivatives, and prediction markets, while letting decentralized lending protocols manage collateral risks outside conventional market hours.
Aave, which had more than $34 billion in total value locked at the service's launch, is adopting the infrastructure through Horizon, its institutional lending platform, initially targeting tokenized US equities.
The expansion also affects LINK's economics.
Fidelity's ETF prospectus identifies demand for Chainlink's services as a factor influencing LINK's value, noting that the network converts certain fees paid in fiat currencies and other digital assets into LINK through its Payment Abstraction mechanism.
While Fidelity's expansion creates another avenue for investment demand, Chainlink's ability to generate additional fee-paying activity from always-on financial markets could provide a separate source of demand for its token.

articles.title: Bitcoin’s $60,000 recovery masks a growing threat that could push its price as low as $29,000
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Bitcoin reclaimed $60,000 after a volatile week that saw it break a historical recovery pattern dating back to 2011.
- Galaxy Research found that Bitcoin has exceeded historical bear market timelines while meeting just two of 13 historical bottom indicators.
- A break below $58,525 could expose Bitcoin to deeper losses, with historical comparisons pointing to levels as low as $28,200.
Bitcoin recovered above $60,000 after slipping below that mark on Nov. 25, in a volatile week in which Bitcoin fell to around $55,000, its lowest level since September 2024.
BTC rebounded to $63,000 on Monday, but subsequently surrendered much of those gains.
According to Talos, Bitcoin lost 7.9% over the week, compared with declines of 2.9% for the S&P 500, 4.5% for the Nasdaq 100 and 7.8% for gold. Over 30 days, Bitcoin has fallen 25.3%, approximately 2.6 times the Nasdaq 100's decline.
Bitcoin's correlation with traditional risk assets has also strengthened. Its 30-day correlations with the S&P 500, Nasdaq 100 and Nvidia climbed to 0.78, 0.77 and 0.68, respectively, roughly 1.4 to twice their one-year medians.
Galaxy Research noted that Bitcoin's recent struggles are particularly unusual given its September recovery above the 50-week moving average, which has historically helped identify the end of bear markets.
Bitcoin has since fallen below both its 50-week and 200-week moving averages, breaking a recovery pattern that had held since 2011.
The four-year cycle faces a historical test
Bitcoin reclaimed its 50-week moving average in September after spending 44 consecutive weeks below it. It held above the indicator for seven weeks, reaching a daily close of $86,521 on Oct. 4, nearly 48% above its June low.
Galaxy found that none of the seven previous recoveries that sustained the moving average for at least seven weeks later produced a new bear-market low, even intraday.
September's recovery differed from earlier instances in one significant respect. Previous recoveries after prolonged periods below the moving average followed declines of 76.7% to 92.7%, whereas September's followed a comparatively shallow 53% drawdown on a closing basis.
Bitcoin's subsequent decline to $55,100 on Nov. 21 prompted Galaxy to withdraw its October assessment that the bear market ended in June.
The breakdown shifts attention to Bitcoin's June 30 closing low of $58,525.
Galaxy identified seven completed instances in which Bitcoin closed below a bear market low that had held for at least 60 days and from which the cryptocurrency had rebounded at least 20%.
All seven resulted in further declines of at least 17.1%, with a median loss of 51.8%. Applied to Bitcoin's June closing low, those historical outcomes would put the cryptocurrency at approximately $48,500 and $28,200, respectively.
However, another closing low would push Bitcoin beyond the historical duration of its bear markets.
As of Nov. 22, 412 days had elapsed since Bitcoin reached its record closing price of $124,824 in October 2025. Its four previous bear markets took between 163 and 406 days to bottom.
The current downturn has also exceeded historical halving-to-bottom timelines. The three previous cycle lows occurred between 777 and 912 days after their respective halvings, compared with the 946 days since Bitcoin's April 2024 halving.
While those timelines suggest Bitcoin is overdue for a recovery, its valuation and investor behavior point toward an unfinished bear market.
BTC investors have yet to capitulate
Bitcoin's previous four bear markets recorded peak-to-trough closing-price declines of approximately 93%, 85%, 84% and 77%, respectively.
Successive downturns have become shallower, but the largest reduction between previous cycles was eight percentage points. A bottom at the June closing low would represent a 24% reduction.
The divergence extends to Bitcoin's realized price, which estimates the aggregate cost basis of its circulating supply.
During previous bear markets, Bitcoin spent between 140 and 304 days below its realized price. It has yet to register a single daily close below that level, which stood at $53,205 on Nov. 22.
Meanwhile, the proportion of Bitcoin's supply held at a loss reached 57% on Nov. 20, within the 55% to 61% range recorded at previous cycle bottoms.
Despite that financial distress, Bitcoin's 30-day realized losses peaked at just 3.6% of its realized capitalization in February, compared with peaks of 7.3% to 16.7% during previous bear markets.
Investor sentiment has deteriorated more sharply. Galaxy's proprietary Bitcoin Fear & Greed Index fell to 5.2 on Nov. 21, its lowest reading since June 2022 and among the lowest 0.5% of historical readings.
Yet the index has spent just six days at or below 10 during the current downturn, compared with between 12 and 57 days during previous bear markets, including the month following their bottoms.
Derivatives traders have also maintained relatively resilient positioning. Bitcoin perpetual futures funding averaged a positive annualized rate of 4.3% over the seven days through Nov. 22, compared with negative 24.5% shortly after the November 2022 bottom.
As of Nov. 22, Bitcoin satisfied just two of the 13 historical bottom indicators Galaxy tracks.
Where could Bitcoin bottom?
The conflict between BTC's historical cycle duration and the depth of its losses leaves Galaxy examining two potential scenarios.
If cycle timelines prevail, several valuation measures point to potential support between $48,400 and $53,200. These include Bitcoin's realized price, its long-term holder cost basis, and the smallest historical decline following the breakdown of an established bear market low.
A bottom within that range would still represent Bitcoin's shallowest bear market on record.
However, a return to the valuation extremes that characterized previous downturns could push Bitcoin toward levels between $29,100 and $46,100.
Galaxy is also monitoring US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded products, which have shed 71,339 BTC worth $4.95 billion since October. Their holdings have declined to approximately 1.24 million BTC, just 1.5% above their July trough.
A break below that 1.22 million BTC trough, alongside a weekly close below Bitcoin's realized price, would strengthen the case for a deeper downturn.
Conversely, reclaiming the 200-week moving average at $68,159 and subsequently the 50-week average at $74,401 would move Galaxy back toward its October recovery thesis.

articles.title: Walmart’s Black Friday rollout reveals how AI agents could spend money without controlling your wallet
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Walmart shoppers can now purchase Black Friday deals through Meta’s Muse AI assistant without exposing their saved card details.
- Spending limits and transaction-specific authorization tokens allow customers to delegate purchasing authority while retaining control over payment credent
- Walmart plans to expand access to more AI assistants but has not clarified when customers must reconfirm purchases within approved spending limits.
Walmart is allowing shoppers to purchase Black Friday deals through Meta’s AI assistant Muse without sharing their saved card details.
The retailer announced the integration on Nov. 24, expanding its Agent Gateway to allow customers to discover products, build shopping carts, and complete purchases through conversations with Meta’s AI assistant.
Shoppers can ask Muse to find television deals, identify discounted products available for delivery or recommend items based on their preferences. Walmart handles product discovery and checkout through its Gateway, which connects external AI assistants to the retailer’s shopping infrastructure.
To make purchases, shoppers must link their Walmart accounts through a sign-in process that redirects them to the retailer before returning them to Muse.
When adding an item to their cart for the first time, shoppers establish an Agent Profile within their Walmart account and set a spending limit for the assistant.
The profile allows customers to distinguish AI-assisted purchases from other orders in their purchase history. They can also revoke the assistant’s purchasing authority by deleting the profile.
Walmart retains control of payment processing. Under its Agentic Access Terms, only shoppers can designate which saved payment method an AI assistant can use. External agents cannot add cards, change payment preferences or access raw card details, including full card numbers.
Instead, each transaction requires a short-lived authorization token tied to the merchant, shopping cart, purchase amount and session. The token expires upon use, requiring fresh authorization for subsequent transactions.
How much spending authority can shoppers give AI?
The integration builds on Walmart’s Agent Profiles, introduced in October as part of its efforts to give customers greater control over purchases made through AI assistants.
By default, shoppers must approve purchases initiated by an agent. However, they can authorize assistants to complete transactions independently within a predetermined spending limit.
Walmart can still request additional confirmation even when a purchase falls within that limit. Its terms also allow the retailer to intervene when transactions exceed or conflict with a customer’s purchasing preferences.
The arrangement creates a framework for AI assistants to move beyond product recommendations and execute purchases on behalf of consumers without directly controlling their payment credentials.
However, Walmart’s launch announcement did not specify when shoppers using Muse would encounter additional approval requests after granting an assistant purchasing authority.
The retailer plans to extend its Gateway to more applications and AI assistants, potentially expanding the number of platforms through which customers can authorize purchases.
Walmart’s existing return policy applies to purchases completed through Muse, although the company has yet to specify which locations and devices are eligible for the rollout.

articles.title: OpenAI’s Codex helps amateur astronomer uncover two possible planets NASA’s data had missed
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Two amateur astronomers used OpenAI’s Codex and Astra to search millions of stars for previously unidentified planetary candidates.
- Their findings demonstrate how general-purpose AI tools could help independent researchers extract new scientific insights from existing public archives.
- Two promising signals have survived preliminary independent checks, but confirming whether they represent undiscovered planets could take months or years.
An AI-assisted search of NASA's archived telescope data has uncovered two possible planets, with preliminary checks by a professional astronomer recovering both signals.
In a Nov. 24 report, OpenAI detailed how two amateur astronomers used its Codex and Astra tools to search observations of millions of stars for previously overlooked planetary candidates.
Kevin Bond, an OpenAI engineer, used Codex to develop software that detects recurring declines in stellar brightness, a potential indication of a planet passing in front of its host star.
Bond combined existing detection methods into a program that deployed two AI agents. One identified promising signals, while the other subjected those findings to further examination.
Running the software against archived observations of approximately 100,000 stars from NASA's Kepler Space Telescope produced more than 200 signals, including 10 associated with previously confirmed planets.
Vishal Gajjar, an astronomer at the SETI Institute, independently recovered two of Bond's findings.
The first involved a relatively cool star, KIC 5689121, whose brightness declined every 13.8 days. OpenAI said the signal was consistent with a potential planet approximately 2.4 times Earth's diameter. The second, KIC 6691030, exhibited recurring dips every 4.8 days, suggesting a potential planet smaller than Neptune.
Gajjar said:
“Our initial checks are encouraging, and follow-up observations will tell us more.”
AI expands the search for distant planets
While Bond focused on Kepler's archived observations, another amateur astronomer, Ethan Byrd, used OpenAI's Astra to examine telescope data covering approximately 19 million stars.
Byrd developed two searches, including one targeting planetary candidates within habitable zones, where atmospheric conditions could allow liquid water to exist on a planet's surface.
His initial search identified 49 candidates. Byrd has submitted one to researchers working on NASA's Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) mission, and two others are awaiting submission.
Astronomers have used artificial intelligence to identify planets for years. In 2017, NASA announced the discovery of Kepler-90i using a neural network trained to recognize planetary signals in telescope observations.
General-purpose AI tools now let amateur astronomers develop their own detection software and search vast archives for signals earlier searches may have missed.
However, recurring declines in stellar brightness can also result from eclipsing stars or fluctuations in telescope instruments.
Astronomers could investigate Bond's candidates by observing their host stars at the predicted transit intervals and measuring whether gravitational forces from potential orbiting planets cause detectable stellar movement.
Establishing whether either signal represents an undiscovered planet could take months or years, OpenAI said.

articles.title: What Is STX? A Guide to the Leading Bitcoin Beta Asset by Market Cap
articles.text:
This article is brought to you by Stacks.
STX is the native asset of Stacks, a Bitcoin layer where BTC holders earn BTC. It is the largest Bitcoin ecosystem asset by market cap after BTC itself, excluding wrapped BTC, with a market cap of $500.57 million as of 16 November 2026.
Most traders know STX as a Bitcoin beta asset: one whose price tends to move with Bitcoin, often by a larger margin. For STX, that relationship is structural and built into the protocol: miners spend BTC to earn STX from network activity, and every BTC staked on Stacks needs STX locked beside it.
Bitcoin staking went live on Stacks in September 2026, and three staking bonds sold out between September and November. In 2027, the PoX-6 upgrade is set to open staking to anyone, and self-custodial Bitcoin borrowing is set to follow.
This guide explains what STX is, why it moves with Bitcoin, how it powers Bitcoin staking, and why its role is designed to grow as Bitcoin becomes productive capital.
Key Takeaways
- STX is the entry point for Bitcoin capital into productive markets, starting with Bitcoin staking.
- Every BTC staked on Stacks needs STX locked beside it, at a current parameter of 5% of the BTC value.
- Institutions stake BTC on the Bitcoin L1 in their own custody and earn BTC at a 3% target annual yield, fixed for each bond's term.
- Stacks miners spend BTC to mine blocks and earn STX from the network’s economic activity, and that BTC funds the staking yield.
- In 2027, PoX-6 is set to open Bitcoin staking to anyone, and self-custodial borrowing is set to let holders borrow stablecoins against staked BTC.
Why STX Matters: Bitcoin Lacks Capital Markets
Bitcoin is the world's leading digital asset, yet most BTC sits idle because Bitcoin has no native capital markets.
Dollars, by contrast, are productive because holders can earn yield on deposits, borrow against them, and trade them in deep, liquid markets. Bitcoin has historically lacked those yield, credit, and trading markets on its own base layer. Holders who wanted to put their BTC to work usually had to wrap it, bridge it, or hand it to a custodian.
Stacks is building those markets for Bitcoin, with STX as the asset Bitcoin capital pairs with to enter each one.
The first market is Bitcoin staking, live since September 2026, where BTC holders earn BTC by locking STX beside their Bitcoin. Two more are scheduled for 2027: an open auction that lets anyone stake BTC, and borrowing stablecoins against staked BTC. Each new market needs STX to operate, so STX's role expands as more go live.
For BTC holders, this means a way to earn BTC on BTC. For STX holders and traders, it ties the token's role to how much Bitcoin is put to work.
Key milestones:
| Date | Milestone | 
| 2019 | STX offering becomes the first SEC-qualified token offering in US history | 
| 2021 | Proof of Transfer begins paying out BTC to participants | 
| 2024 | Nakamoto upgrade (October) and sBTC launch (December) | 
| September to November 2026 | Bitcoin staking Bonds 1 to 3 sell out | 
| 11 November 2026 | First post-quantum sBTC transfer on mainnet | 
| 2027 | PoX-6 open auction and self-custodial Bitcoin borrowing | 
STX at a Glance
| Item | Detail | 
| Ticker | STX | 
| What it is | Native asset of Stacks, a Bitcoin layer | 
| Roles | Bitcoin staking capacity, miner reward, transaction fees | 
| Staking capacity parameter | 5% of staked BTC value (current) | 
| Bitcoin staking yield | 3% target annual, fixed per bond, earned in BTC | 
| BTC distributed since 2021 | Over 4,200 BTC | 
| Market cap as of 16 November 2026 | $500.57M | 
How STX Powers Bitcoin Staking
Bitcoin staking on Stacks follows three steps: stake BTC on Bitcoin, pair it with STX, and earn BTC.
A participant stakes BTC on the Bitcoin L1, in their own custody. Alongside it, they lock STX worth a set share of the BTC value for the bond's term. The current parameter is 5%.
In return, participants earn BTC. The current bonds carry a 3% target annual yield, fixed for each bond's term. Today, participation runs through institutional bonds, with custody and infrastructure support from BitGo, Anchorage Digital, Fireblocks, and Fordefi. Open participation is planned for 2027 through PoX-6.
Because every staked BTC needs STX beside it, demand for STX as staking capacity is linked to how much Bitcoin wants to earn, so more BTC staked means more STX locked.
What a Staking Position Looks Like
The example below is illustrative and uses the current parameters.
| Item | Amount | 
| BTC staked | 100 BTC | 
| STX locked beside it (5% of BTC value) | STX worth 5 BTC | 
| Target annual yield (3%) | 3 BTC over one year | 
The yield is a target, not a guarantee, and the 5% parameter can change for future bonds.
The Consensus Mechanism That Ties Stacks to Bitcoin
Stacks uses a consensus mechanism called Proof of Transfer. Miners spend BTC for the chance to mine Stacks blocks, and they earn STX from emissions and transaction fees in return..
That BTC is paid out as yield to staked Bitcoin, so the staking yield exists because miners want STX. Since 2021, Stacks has distributed over 4,200 BTC in rewards to participants.
This is the structural relationship behind STX's Bitcoin beta: its role is tied directly to Bitcoin activity, through miners spending BTC and stakers pairing STX with BTC.
STX has three roles in the network:
- Staking capacity: STX locked beside BTC sets how much Bitcoin can be staked.
- Miner reward: miners earn STX for producing Stacks blocks, paid for in BTC.
- Fees: STX pays for every transaction and app on Stacks.
What STX Becomes: The Entry Point to Bitcoin Capital Markets
Stacks' goal is for Bitcoin capital to enter each new market by pairing with STX as that market goes live.
Three Bitcoin staking bonds sold out between September and November 2026, with 1735 BTC staked across them. Participants include 21shares, Bullish, UTXO Management, HashKey Cloud, and Sypher Capital.
In 2027, PoX-6 is set to introduce an open auction that lets anyone stake BTC through a self-custodial path. STX bids in that auction would set how much BTC can be staked.
Self-custodial Bitcoin borrowing is in research and development for 2027. Holders will be able to borrow stablecoins against staked BTC while it keeps earning. Because the loan sits on top of a staked position, the same STX capacity supports both staking and borrowing. Thanks to the bidding mechanism, Stacks enabling both earning BTC from staking and using it as collateral for borrowing would increase the earning potential of Bitcoin capital deployment, likely resulting in higher STX bids under PoX-6.
The borrowed capital from using the staked BTC as collateral, such as stablecoins, could be used to spend, lend, trade in the markets available through Stacks. Financial applications such as Zest and Bitflow use STX as the rails for this capital inflow to be made productive. Every transaction on the network is secured by 100% of Bitcoin’s security budget, making transactions on Stacks as irreversible as Bitcoin’s.
| Market | Status | Role of STX | 
| Bitcoin staking | Live | Staking capacity locked beside BTC | 
| Bitcoin apps (Zest, Bitflow, Hermetica) | Live | Pays transaction fees | 
| PoX-6 open auction | R&D ~2027 | STX bids set how much BTC can be staked | 
| Self-custodial Bitcoin borrowing | R&D ~2027 | Staked BTC backs stablecoin loans on the same STX bids, increasing the value for capital it unlocks | 
How to Get STX
STX trades on major centralized exchanges, including Binance, Coinbase, OKX, Kraken, Gate, Bullish and more. To see current trading pairs, volumes, and prices, check the Markets tab on the STX page on Coingecko.
Investors who prefer traditional brokerage access can also look at exchange-traded products. 21shares and Valour both offer STX ETPs, which are available on select European exchanges.
Before buying, compare fees, liquidity, and withdrawal options across venues.
Frequently Asked Questions
What is STX used for?
STX has three main uses. It is locked beside BTC as Bitcoin staking capacity, it is the reward miners earn for producing Stacks blocks, and it pays fees for every transaction and app on Stacks.
Why does STX move with Bitcoin?
The link is built into the protocol. Miners spend BTC to earn STX, and every staked BTC needs STX locked beside it. Both tie STX's role directly to Bitcoin activity.
Do I need STX to stake Bitcoin?
Yes. To stake BTC on Stacks, a participant locks STX alongside it for the bond's term. The current parameter is STX worth 5% of the BTC value.
Where does the BTC yield come from?
The yield comes from Stacks miners. They spend BTC to mine Stacks blocks and earn STX, and that BTC is paid out to staked Bitcoin. The current bonds target 3% a year, fixed per bond.
Does my BTC leave the Bitcoin blockchain when I stake?
No. BTC is staked on the Bitcoin L1 and stays in the participant's own custody.
What changes for STX with PoX-6?
PoX-6, planned for 2027, is set to open Bitcoin staking to anyone through an open auction. STX bids in that auction will set how much BTC can be staked.
The Bottom Line
STX's link to BTC is structural: miners spend BTC to earn STX, that BTC funds the staking yield, and every staked BTC needs STX locked beside it.
Bitcoin staking is the first live market built on that design. Three bonds sold out in 2026, and institutions are now earning BTC on BTC without moving it off the Bitcoin L1.
With PoX-6 and self-custodial borrowing research and development planned for 2027, Stacks aims to make STX the asset Bitcoin capital pairs with to enter each new market, from staking to borrowing and trading. If Bitcoin becomes productive capital, STX is positioned at the entry point.
Stacks is where Bitcoin earns. Learn more about Bitcoin staking at stacks.co.
